LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 10 picks, including the Packers to spoil Kirk Cousins' return with the Vikings Imagn Images A perfect week. Can you believe it? I went 15-0 with my straight-up picks last week. I guess it was an easy week, like some said. As for my picks against the spread, it wasn't quite as good, but it was better than it's been. I went 9-6 for the week, which I will take. The season marks are now 59-74-3 ATS and 87-48-1 straight up. Let's see if we can get perfect against the spread this week. Yeah, right. I will take three games above. 500 again as I make the climb to respectability. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Giants are back home after beating the Eagles and now face a Commanders team that probably has to win this to have any chance at the playoffs. The Giants' defense has been dominant up front as of late, and that will continue here as they contain Jayden Daniels . Giants keep winning. Pick: Giants 23, Commanders 14 New England Patriots at Detroit Lions (-2.5) Munich on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a big game for both teams, but especially so for the Patriots after they got blown out by the Packers at home last week. The Lions won at Miami and didn't play great, but they will get it going on offense here. New England is struggling on defense, so look for the Lions to win it with a strong offensive showing. Pick: Lions 30, Patriots 24 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs snapped a two-game losing streak last week in beating the Jets , while the Falcons were blown out in Madrid by the Bengals . The defense had some major issues in that game. That will be the same here after the trade of safety Jessie Bates. Chiefs stack another victory. Pick: Chiefs 23, Falcons 17 Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns (+4.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns . But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. Pick: Texans 21, Browns 20 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) The Packers are coming off an impressive road victory over the Patriots and Jordan Love has been on fire. But the Minnesota defense is special and now they have Kirk Cousins to play quarterback. Even so, look for the Packers to win another one as their defense limits Cousins and the offense. Pick: Packers 27, Vikings 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-10.5) at Tennessee Titans The Titans are coming off a bye, while the Jaguars are coming off a victory last Thursday at Baltimore. They will be rested too. Jacksonville is riding high as one of the top teams in the league and made some moves at the trade deadline to get even better. Though this is a rivalry, with some unpredictable games, this won't be. Jaguars big. Pick: Jaguars 31, Titans 17 Miami Dolphins (+3.5) at Indianapolis Colts This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. Pick: Colts 23, Dolphins 22 Carolina Panthers at New Orleans Saints (-2.5) This is an enormous game in the division, even though both teams have just three victories. The winner will be in first place. The Saints beat the Browns last week, while the Panthers have lost three straight. The Saints make it four in a row as Tyler Shough has a big day. Pick: Saints 24, Panthers 21 Buffalo Bills (-8.5) at New York Jets The Bills are coming off a hard-fought road victory at Minnesota. The turnaround will be tough, but they are playing at a high level. The defense is improving. Look for Josh Allen to carve up the Jets' defense. Pick: Bills 34, Jets 21 Seattle Seahawks (-6.5) at Las Vegas Raiders Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Seahawks will start Drew Lock at quarterback again in this one. He was just OK last week against Arizona. But the Raiders have big-time defensive issues. For the Raiders, it's Fernando Mendoza time after they traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota. This is a tough defense for a first NFL start. Look for Lock to win it as the Seahawks' defense does the rest. Pick: Seahawks 24, Raiders 16 Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals (+9.5) The Rams lost at home to the Cardinals a few weeks ago and now must play without Puka Nacua . How will they move the ball? The Cardinals will start rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Going against Myles Garrett and company can be a problem. Rams win it, but it's low-scoring. Pick: Rams 19, Cardinals 16 San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys (+4.5) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys can't afford another loss in their division race, so this is a huge game for them. The 49ers are riding high and that offense will challenge the Dallas defense. But I think the Dallas offense will be even better. Upset special. Dak Prescott has a bigger day than Brock Purdy . Pick: Cowboys 30, 49ers 28 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is for first place in the division. The Bengals are riding high behind their passing game and Joe Burrow . But the defense can't stop the run. The Steelers will run it here to keep Burrow off the field. It doesn't work. The Bengals will once again win it behind Burrow and the passing game. Pick: Bengals 27, Steelers 21 Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) at Baltimore Ravens Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This game had promise before the season, but the Ravens are without Lamar Jackson and the Chargers are 0-8. Jacoby Brissett will start for the Ravens, which should help the offense some. The Chargers have struggled on offense, but I think their defense will keep them in this. It's close. These teams tied in their first meeting of the 2026 season, setting up an interesting battle on Thursday with the head-to-head tiebreaker at stake. New York (5-2-1) has a three-game lead over Washington in the NFC East, but the Dallas Cowboys (4-5) at least have a shot to catch the Giants this season. So, who is favored to win on Thursday? The latest odds continue to move in favor of the Giants, who are expected to have J.J. McCarthy (hip pointer) under center in this game. Commanders vs. Giants Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Commanders +2.5 (-110) Giants -2.5 (-110) Commanders: +120 41.5 (Over -105/Under -115) The odds for this game have moved towards New York in multiple ways. After the Giants opened as 1.5-point favorites on Sunday night , they are now favored by 2.5 and have much better moneyline odds to win this game. New York has shifted all the way up to -142 to win , as 62 percent of the moneyline bets and 69 percent of the spread bets at DraftKings are on Harbaugh's team. There has also been a slight change in the odds associated with the total. The OVER was (-112) on Tuesday, but that has since moved to -105 with the UNDER now favored. The total remains at 41.5 for this NFC East battle even though these teams combined for 54 points in their tie back in Week 5. A win on Thursday would go a long way for a Giants team that is looking to win the division even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) sidelined. Meanwhile, Washington's chance to win the division hinges a lot on this game, as a loss would put Daniels and Co. four games back of New York without the tiebreaker this season. Earlier this week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite pick for every game in Week 10 in his Road to 272 column . He’s targeting New York as a home favorite to cover: I may have included the New York Giants in last week's edition of my Fraud Rankings , but my biggest issue with them has been their strength of schedule. Will I be betting on them when they take on teams like the Jaguars and 49ers in the coming weeks? Likely not, but they once again have a game against a bad team on Thursday Night Football when they face the Washington Commanders, and much like the majority of the season, I expect them to take care of business against an inferior opponent. These two teams played to a tie in Week 5 earlier this season, but with it being a road game for the Giants and the fact that they had Jameis Winston at quarterback, I think we can admit they're in a better spot in the rematch. J.J. McCarthy has been surprisingly solid to begin his tenure with the Giants, ranking fifth in the NFL in completion percentage over expected (+5.3%) amongst quarterbacks who have played 60+ snaps this season. It's also no coincidence that over the last three weeks, the Giants have led the league in net yards per play at +1.5. Meanwhile, the Commanders continue to be a poorly coached team that doesn't thrive in any area, ranking in the bottom half of the NFL in virtually every metric. Washington is coming off a 20-13 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, while the Giants are coming off a 19-11 road win against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Commanders are averaging 21.5 points per game with a points-per-game differential of -3.75. The Giants have fared a little better, averaging 22.8 points per game with a 1.25-point-per-game differential. Just one of their wins (Week 4 vs. Arizona) has been by 10 points or more, which means the Giants have squeaked by so far. The good news for the Giants is their defense has been dominant. New York has allowed just 172 points to opponents this season, the seventh-lowest mark in the league, making a valid argument that the defense has carried the team for most of the season. What will this week bring? Let’s take a look. Another Divisional Win? Please. The Giants have not beaten Washington since 2023. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants erased the 13-year losing streak in Philadelphia on Sunday. away.headline: Commanders-Rams final injury report rules out two receivers, leaves McDuffie questionable
away.blurb: The Washington Commanders released their final injury report Friday ahead of their matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The report listed two of Washington's receivers, Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf), as officially OUT against the Rams. Burks missed practice all week with an injured foot that he's been dealing with since the 49ers game, while Brown was added to Thursday's report as limited before missing Friday's practice. With Terry McLaurin already out for the season, Washington will need more from Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, who led the team with seven targets and five catches for 54 yards against Philadelphia . Van Jefferson could see more work, and Luke McCaffrey is another option. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn spoke Friday about Jefferson's readiness: "I liked his approach. I liked his readiness, and so when called upon, I'd expect he'd play well." Rookie Jaden Bradley could also be elevated from the practice squad, although Washington hasn't announced that move. Elsewhere on the report, Jer'Zhan Newton is questionable with his pectoral injury despite practicing fully all three days. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window and must be activated from injured reserve before he can play. That decision carries some weight with Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw now on IR . Shy Tuttle (shoulder) was limited all week but carries no game designation, while Sam Cosmi (knee) returned to full participation Friday. John Bates (shoulder) was limited throughout the week but has no game designation either. Los Angeles has some injury problems of its own, particularly in the secondary . Cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) is out, while Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable after missing every practice this week. Former Commanders safety Kam Curl (foot) is also questionable after returning to limited practice Friday. The Rams could be short-handed in the secondary, although McDuffie's and Curl's availability won't be settled until closer to kickoff. The Rams also listed long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) as doubtful, with tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), and receiver Jordan Whittington (back) questionable. Quarterback Matthew Stafford practiced fully throughout the week, while head coach Sean McVay expects Myles Garrett to play Sunday, pending his activation from injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) was ruled out after injuring his hamstring in Friday’s practice . McCarthy made it clear on Tuesday that he will be able to play on Thursday night against the Washington Commanders after suffering a hip injury in Week 9. McCarthy's comments come after ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Monday that the Giants were "confident" he would be able to play. McCarthy took a hard hit while running during a play in Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles. He went to the sidelines at first and attempted to test it with a throw but winced in pain while falling to a knee. New York, of course, already lost Jaxson Dart to injury this season. The Giants traded for McCarthy in part as a response to Dart's injury, and the Michigan product played well in his immediate game action for the NFC East team. He threw for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception during the fourth quarter of a game against the New Orleans Saints and earned the start in the ensuing matchup against the Houston Texans. Despite being on the road against a Texans defense with a number of headline players, McCarthy led the Giants to an overtime victory by throwing for 252 yards, zero touchdowns and zero interceptions. There was little question after that performance he would be the starter for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles, although it did not go as well for him even before the injury. away.headline: Rams Injury Report, Week 9 at Commanders: Myles Garrett expected to play; Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl questionable; Terrance Ferguson ruled out
away.blurb: Rams Injury Report, Week 9 at Commanders: Myles Garrett expected to play; Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl questionable; Terrance Ferguson ruled out Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM "We're still working through those types of things," McVay said Friday morning prior to practice, when asked what kind of ramp-up he expects in terms of how much Garrett is able to play on Sunday. "He's really done a great job in practice. He'll be a DNP today, but it's more of just being smart with him. Nothing to do with anything other than he has progressed really well, made a tremendous impact in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, feels really comfortable with the game plan, and it's been great having him out there, as well as (tight end) Terrance (Ferguson)." While Ferguson (ankle) also returned to practice this week, and was expected to play Sunday according to McVay, he ended up being ruled out after the Rams sent out an updated injury report. Initially listed on this week's report with an ankle injury, Ferguson picked up a hamstring injury in Friday's practice based on the injury updated report. Meanwhile, Trent McDuffie (back) and tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) are listed as questionable for Sunday's game, as well as inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and safety Kam Curl (foot). Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) is listed as doubtful, which would set up Jake McQuaide to be up from the practice squad again. McVay also said cornerback Jaylen Watson is listed as out, but will be placed on IR. Otherwise, all other Rams players listed on the injury report do not have a game status designation. For the Commanders, wide receivers Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf) have been ruled out, while defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) is listed as questionable. New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy exited the team's Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles after taking a massive hit from linebacker Zack Baun. He eventually returned to the game after a trip to the locker room, but the team has since revealed if it could affect his playing status moving forward. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN , McCarthy suffered a hip pointer and the team is confident that he will be ready for Thursday night’s game against the Washington Commanders. That is certainly good news, given how the injury initially looked. He was in visible pain on the sideline before heading to the locker room and being replaced by backup quarterback Jameis Winston. The Giants traded a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy following starter Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury in September. New York then switched to McCarthy as its starter ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans, and he has played quite well since, throwing for 622 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

This week, Philadelphia will be thin at wide receiver once again. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were both ruled out for Sunday's game , leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, and Hollywood Brown to take on the bulk of the receiving work. Giants could take huge steps to clinching the NFC East after return from bye week Injuries are a part of life in the NFL. No team is immune to the inevitable knocks that players take throughout the season. But it's hard not to feel like the New York Giants have had an unfortunate run of injury luck this year. Three of the most important players on the roster (Jaxson Dart, Brian Burns, and Tremaine Edmunds) have already sustained season-ending injuries. Both offensive tackles have been banged up at various points. Still, Big Blue sits atop the NFC East heading into a critical matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 9 . The injury woes haven't stopped, though. The G-Men could be without Cam Skattebo for this game, leaving their running back room alarmingly thin. With Friday's practice reports in the books, let's check in on the status of a couple of the Giants' most important injuries. Giants' final injury report before Week 9 Eagles matchup Skattebo suffered a hamstring injury during his long run in overtime against the Houston Texans. He put his body on the line for the win, literally. Even after the bye week, he still isn't trending toward playing on Sunday. If Skattebo doesn't play, the weight of the running back room will be placed on the shoulders of veteran Devin Singletary and rookie UDFA Greg Desrosiers Jr . In all likelihood, Phil Mafah would be promoted to the active roster to add a third option. Game Status: No Injury Designation After spending the entire offseason wondering about his recovery from the knee injury that ended his 2025 campaign, it was gut-wrenching to see Malik Nabers pop up on the injury report with a knee issue again. No need to worry, though; It looks like he'll be just fine. Nabers didn't practice on Thursday, but he was a full participant on Friday and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game. It's a good thing he's ready to go, because the G-Men haven't found much production from the rest of their receiver room. As encouraging as Malachi Fields' progression has been, nobody wants to see him take on WR1 responsibilities against this Eagles secondary. All things considered, the Giants' injury report has been mostly positive this week. Skattebo may not suit up, but for the most part, this will be the same team that took down the Texans. The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It's been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it'll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots' 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers' worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: "Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven't turned the ball over, they haven't exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it's just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven't quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error." The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

picks.headline: Lions-Patriots preview: Can New England bounce back from ugly loss?
picks.blurb: Lions-Patriots preview: Can New England bounce back from ugly loss? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline grades Latest CFP rankings Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers NFL trade deadline tracker Vikings trade for Cousins Lions-Patriots preview: Can New England bounce back from ugly loss? Jacob Richman · MLive.com Wed, November 11, 2026 at 11:01 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions take their four-game winning streak international in Week 10, heading to Munich, Germany to face the New England Patriots in a Sunday morning kickoff for fans back in Detroit. The Lions (6-2) are finding some strong consistency with their defense after a slow start and hope to keep putting the pressure on the Patriots (5-4), who are coming off a rough loss to the Green Bay Packers. This is just the second crack at the Patriots that the Lions have had since coach Dan Campbell took over and that 2022 matchup isn't one to remember after Detroit was shut out in a lopsided defeat. Both teams are in different places now and each will be eager to get a win out in Germany as playoff contenders that are currently chasing the lead in their respective divisions. Here's a preview of the Lions' Week 10 opponent, the New England Patriots: Three players to know If there's a player to watch for how this matchup might go, it's cornerback Christian Gonzalez . The 24-year-old inked a four-year, $135 million contract extension with the Patriots and was largely playing well until this past week when he had a historically terrible game. Gonzalez allowed seven catches for 105 yards to Packers receiver Matthew Golden and another 82 yards on three catches to Christian Watson. He's the first defender, as far back as Next Gen Stats go — at least 2018 — to allow more than 80 receiving yards in coverage to two players in the same game. That is not the same Gonzalez that has been the anchor of the Patriots defense the past few years. A bounce-back performance for the active cornerback would mean a long day for Detroit's offense, but if he's struggling in the same way as last week, it could be a field day for the Lions. The Patriots have experienced a brutal amount of injuries to their skill position players. Fortunately for New England, wide receiver DeMario Douglas has really stepped up in place of the many missing contributors on offense. He's accumulated 434 yards on 31 catches with a career-high four touchdowns. Douglas went for 100 yards for the first time this season last week and is on pace to set a career-high for yardage, if he can stay healthy. Even though A.J. Brown is traveling to Germany, it doesn't appear he'll be ready to go, meaning another game Douglas is likely the primary target in the passing attack. New England found another defensive gem in edge rusher Elijah Ponder , who came to the franchise as an undrafted free agent in 2025 out of FCS Cal Poly. Ponder was solid as a rookie with four sacks and 24 total tackles. His second season is already looking like a true breakout as Ponder has 25 total tackles, 7.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a pass breakup through nine games. Ponder leads the Patriots with 32 total pressures this season, which is top-15 in the NFL. He is quickly becoming one of the top young edges in the league and someone the Lions are going to need to be very cognizant of on Sunday. Quarterback corner The season certainly hasn't gone as expected for third-year quarterback Drake Maye after an incredible sophomore season where the former third overall pick threw for 4,394 yards, 31 touchdowns and eight picks on a league-leading 72% completion, while taking the Patriots to an appearance at Super Bowl LX. The 24-year-old returned with MVP-level expectations and a new top receiver coming in with veteran A.J. Brown. However, the year has been chaotic for Maye, already throwing a career-high 11 interceptions with 2,282 yards and 18 touchdowns. This season, Maye's only completed over 70% of his passes three times, compared to 11 times last season and hasn't had Brown available outside three games due to injury. He's coming off a rough night against the Packers where he did manage to throw for 299 yards and three touchdowns, but also completed just 55.3% of his passes, had three picks and was sacked four times in an 18-point home loss. It's clear Maye isn't looking like the same player who was runner-up for MVP last season. But he's certainly not a quarterback to be taken lightly, because if he finds his rhythm, he's capable of picking apart any defense. Keys to success Win the turnover battle: With Maye tied for the NFL lead in interceptions and the Patriots giving up another eight fumbles, the problem on offense has been pretty clear — they're not having nearly enough possessions. And the New England defense only has five picks and three fumble recoveries on the season. When the offense is valuing possession and the defense is forcing takeaways, it's really shown in the results. The Patriots are 5-1 when turning the ball over two or fewer times in a game. They are also winless in games where they fail to record a turnover on the defensive side. Even though there are a lot of things to like about New England's defense, the unit has really struggled to rebound when the offense gives the ball away. Following the 19 combined turnovers the Patriots have committed, the other team has scored on the ensuing drive 13 times this season. Cleaning this up on both sides seems to be the easiest path for the Patriots this season, a bit of a tough break going against a Lions defense with an interception in each of the last four games and an offense with five total turnovers for the season. Make the Lions one-dimensional: The Patriots have a top-10 run defense that can really jam up the field for an opposing running back. The Lions have Jahmyr Gibbs, the best back New England's faced this year, but even so the Patriots will try and keep his impact negligible and likely attempt to get Detroit in a lot of passing situations and be able to commit more numbers into coverage. The Lions have a diverse offense that can beat an opponent in a lot of different ways, but if New England can dictate on early downs, it's going to make it a real challenge to move the ball effectively the way teams that have beat the Patriots often manage to. One big question Is New England primed for a bounce-back performance? While the Patriots had a more lopsided loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season, something about last week's defeat really seemed to hit that locker room hard. Players like Douglas spoke about the team feeling disconnected and needing to figure out how to band together. That's an area the Lions don't seem to be having any issues with, right now. That alone can be the difference in a game, but not if an approaching .500 record and the rising urgency of getting dominated on their own home field can get the Patriots to start cleaning up their play. Dealing with the international travel and continuing injuries aren't going to be helpful for the Patriots, but the Lions are going through them all the same. However, the Lions are coming into the game on four straight wins and New England needs to start up a new winning streak to avoid getting lost in the AFC playoff conversation. There's no doubt that the Patriots have enough talent to win any game on their schedule — as the Lions do — but they're at what could be a very key moment in terms of starting to turn things around from an inconsistent start when the two teams meet up in Germany. away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Star wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson have already been ruled out for the game. The Patriots might also be missing tight end Hunter Henry, who is still battling the foot injury he suffered in last week's win over the Miami Dolphins. Veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins and interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten both returned from injured reserve this week to practice. They are officially listed as questionable to play against the Packers. The New England Patriots will once again be shorthanded on the offensive side of the ball when hosting the Green Bay Packers for a visit on Sunday. But it isn't all bad news for the Patriots. Hollins has been one of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's most reliable downfield targets, and Van Roten was the top replacement at right guard behind Mike Onwenu. Those returns would be a huge lift to a Patriots offense that needs all of the help it can get. away.headline: Patriots face running back crisis before Munich after Rhamondre Stevenson injury
away.source: New England Sports Network (NESN) on MSN
away.blurb: Running back Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to miss multiple weeks with an injury involving the plantaris tendon behind his knee, according to reports attributed to NFL Network's Ian Rapopor t and ESPN's Adam Schefter. The injury occurred during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers, when Stevenson exited in the second half and did not return. The reported absence is particularly concerning because TreVeyon Henderson has also been unavailable. That leaves the Patriots potentially relying on two less-experienced options during a difficult stretch of their schedule. Corey Kiner appears positioned for an expanded role if Stevenson and Henderson remain unavailable. Lan Larison is another option, particularly in passing situations. New England also has Terrell Jennings available on its practice squad if additional depth becomes necessary. New England's next practice reports should clarify which backs are available. For now, a position that appeared reasonably deep earlier in the season has become one of the team's biggest concerns heading to Germany. The New England Patriots are preparing for their first regular-season game in Munich, but their backfield could look dramatically different when they face the Detroit Lions on Sunday. Stevenson Has Been More Than A Runner Stevenson has carried the ball 102 times for 399 yards and two touchdowns this season, but his contributions extend beyond rushing production. He also has 26 receptions for 258 yards and two receiving touchdowns, providing Drake Maye with a dependable outlet in the passing game. Stevenson has handled approximately 65% of New England's offensive snaps, reflecting the importance of his role in multiple personnel packages. His pass protection is another element the Patriots must replace. Losing a running back who understands blitz pickups can affect the entire offense, particularly when the offensive line is already dealing with injuries. Corey Kiner Could Receive His Biggest Opportunity Kiner has rushed for 244 yards and a touchdown on 50 carries, averaging 4.9 yards per attempt. Those numbers suggest he can provide productive rushing plays, although a larger workload would test his consistency and ability to handle different assignments. MORE : Tom Brady Gives Blunt Assessment of Patriots Midway Through Season The Patriots must prepare for Detroit while managing international travel and a short window to reorganize their backfield. Maye threw three interceptions against Green Bay, making offensive balance especially important as New England attempts to rebound. A dependable rushing attack could reduce the pressure on its quarterback, but that task becomes more difficult without Stevenson. away.headline: A.J. Brown Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Return Timeline Amid Patriots' 'Optimistic' Outlook
away.blurb: The quick turnaround between the games may have put additional stress on Brown's knee, but the Patriots are "optimistic" he could return after the team's Week 11 bye, according to Pelissero. New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss his second consecutive game due to a knee injury that has hampered him throughout his career, but the team isn't down on his prospects, insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday. The Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick to acquire Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason, but the results have been underwhelming through the first half of the season. Brown suffered an ankle injury during the team's regular-season opener against the Seattle Seahawks. The 29-year-old returned from a stint on the injured reserve list in Week 6, and he played four days later when the Patriots faced the Chicago Bears on Thursday Night Football. Then, Brown popped up on the injury report with a knee issue. The Los Angeles Rams were also interested in trading for Brown during the offseason, but they were reportedly scared off by the medical concerns with his knee, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported. New England head coach Mike Vrabel, who drafted Brown during his time as head coach of the Tennessee Titans, was evidently more comfortable with the medical evaluations. Brown has only caught passes in each of the three games he played in this season, bringing his tally up to nine receptions for 101 yards and no touchdowns. There was belief that the eight-year veteran would be a great fit as a vertical threat for quarterback Drake Maye, who has been one of the best deep-ball passers in the league. That hasn't proven to be the case: Brown is only averaging 8.3 yards per catch — significantly down from his career average of 15.3 yards per reception. home.blurb: Aidan Hutchinson told CBS Sports' Melanie Collins that it wasn't hard to get motivated this week, pointing out that it was weird without Jack Campbell in meetings. Campbell's medical diagnosis has not yet been made public. Medical experts reached by USA TODAY did point out the uniqueness of Campbell's post-injury symptoms, saying that delayed recovery of upper-body movement could be associated with central cord syndrome . It's a rare medical condition common in people with spinal injuries who have fallen forward and land on their forehead and extend backward, similar to the action exhibited by Campbell’s head and neck at impact. A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 and received the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football. Campbell slid right in as a key piece of the Lions' defense after arriving in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season. The Detroit Lions took the field in Week 9 against the Miami Dolphins without a key member of their defense – Jack Campbell. It marked the Lions' first contest since the linebacker suffered a terrifying neck injury during the team's Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings . The injury left Campbell laying on the field motionless before being carted off the field on a backboard as emotional teammates looked on . Campbell issued a statement about his condition on Wednesday, Nov. 4. He said that he has movement in his lower body and was making progress towards regaining movement in his upper body. It was an encouraging update that extended beyond the generic ones provided earlier in the week . From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. The Lions escaped Miami with a 19-9 win over the Dolphins, but it was clear that Jack Campbell was still top of mind. "A lot of what we said was win No. 6 for 46," Dan Campbell told reporters . "And we did that today. We got that done." It's a reminder that Campbell has a long way to go in his recovery, but he remains determined to get back on the field, according to CBS Sports' Melanie Collins. "He is determined to get back on this football field, telling Dan Campbell: 'Just make sure the house is taken care of until I can get back,'" Collins reported on the CBS broadcast of the game. away.headline: Report: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes avoids major elbow injury
away.blurb: "Patrick took a pretty good shot to the throwing arm today and came off the field in some pain. We checked him out right away and he told us his elbow was sore, but he was determined to get back out there," Reid said. "He returned, made some throws, and kept competing the way he always does. He's one of the toughest players I've ever coached, and he doesn't like missing snaps." Nov 09 (Field Level Media) - Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided a major injury to his right elbow, according to a media report Sunday night. An MRI exam revealed an elbow strain or sprain but no significant damage, NFL Network reported. Mahomes will be monitored for pain and swelling over the next few days, leaving his status uncertain for next Sunday's game against the host Atlanta Falcons. Mahomes injured his throwing arm during Kansas City's 35-12 victory over the New York Jets. He completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns but said afterward that his arm did not feel right early in the second half. "From the stories you hear, whenever you can grab the ball and try to throw it, you can't throw," Mahomes said. "Once I threw the football, I knew it wasn't -- hopefully, I haven't done the test yet -- it wasn't ligament-type stuff, it was more muscle-type stuff." Mahomes was drilled by Jets rookie edge rusher David Bailey while raring back to fire a pass downfield with 1:33 left in the first half. He came off the field supporting his right elbow with his left arm and appeared to be in significant pain. Head coach Andy Reid said the Chiefs would follow all of the proper steps to confirm Mahomes is not hurt. If upcoming tests give the Chiefs pause, Reid said the plan will be to "prepare Justin (Fields)" to face the Falcons on Sunday. Fields did not attempt a pass Sunday but ran twice for minus-1 yard. Mahomes returned to start Week 1 after sustaining a season-ending left knee injury in 2025.

That leaves no verified reason to describe Chase as injured. The report instead points toward normal availability, though the inactive list will not be final until game day. The performance pushed his 2026 totals to 43 catches for 492 yards, and he has six touchdowns through seven games, according to NFL statistics. home.headline: Injured Bengals Defender Good to Go Against Falcons as Team Announces Inactives
home.blurb: Johnson was listed as questionable on the injury report with an ankle/foot designation after suffering the injury in last week’s 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans. Safety Kyle Dugger was ruled out Friday with the quad injury that has forced him to miss three of the last four games. Cornerback DJ Turner II injured his foot last week against the Titans and was limited to start the week, but he did not appear on the injury report and is expected to start and play his full role. Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Cedric Johnson is active for today’s NFL International Game in Madrid against the Atlanta Falcons. The other inactives are offensive tackle Myles Hinton, center Connor Lew and defensive tackle Landon Robinson. The Bengals only need four inactives today because their roster is currently at 52. The Bengals arrived in Madrid on Wednesday and practiced Thursday and Friday to get back on a normal weekly schedule. "I think this is the best compromise we found to make sure that we can get acclimated by Friday, get a really good practice where we feel better, and then play our best on Sunday," head coach Zac Taylor said on Thursday. "So we've all embraced that mindset, and I think it's working well for us so far." "We're back on schedule,” he added. “Our meetings were the same as they've always been on Thursday. So today is more of a third-down emphasis with some normal downs, and then tomorrow will be red zone-based." Quarterback Joe Burrow said he and his teammates are excited to be representing the NFL abroad and about being in a stand-alone window as the only game on Sunday morning. “It means a lot to me that we're here,” he said Friday. “I think this is Year 7 for me, and I haven't been overseas yet. And we keep adding more and more games to try to build the NFL globally. I think it's worked over the last five years, and I'm hoping to add more and continue to build, and I love being part of that, and I want to help grow the game, and so I love being here. "I love being the only game on TV on Sunday morning when people back home wake up, and I love showcasing our talents abroad and trying to bring attention to what we do, as far as what our offense brings. I think we're explosive, we're dynamic, we're fun to watch, and I think we're going to put on a show on Sunday." The team will fly home immediately after the game and, unlike their previous two international games when they had a bye to recover, will start preparations for a key AFC North game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Houston Texans (3-5) head to Cleveland on Sunday looking to continue a dramatic midseason turnaround when they face the Browns (5-4) at Huntington Bank Field. The Texans opened the season with four straight losses but have won three of their last four. The division may be out of reach as the Jaguars lead the Texans by three games in the AFC South but Houston is back in the race for a Wild Card spot. Cleveland takes the field after dropping their last two games which has dropped them out of first in the AFC North and 1.5 games behind the Steelers and the Bengals. Houston is coming off its most explosive performance of the season, a 44-22 road rout of the winless Los Angeles Chargers. C.J. Stroud played through an illness and completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. He connected with four different players for scores, including 63-yard touchdowns to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte , with Boutte finishing with 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The Texans led 24-9 at halftime, stretched the advantage to 38-9 early in the fourth quarter and defensively overwhelmed Justin Herbert , sacking him eight times. Cleveland arrives home following a gut-wrenching 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. With Deshaun Watson sidelined by a concussion, Shedeur Sanders started and finished 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, including a 64-yard go-ahead strike to KC Concepcion late in the fourth quarter. After New Orleans regained the lead, Andre Szmyt’s 51-yard field goal forced overtime. The Saints scored first in the extra period, but Sanders answered by finding Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown before Cleveland went for two and the win; the conversion failed, dropping the Browns to 5-4. The matchup also renews a surprisingly balanced series. Houston leads the all-time matchup 8-7, including the postseason, but Cleveland won four consecutive meetings from 2020 through the 2023 regular season. Their most recent clash reversed that trend in emphatic fashion: in the 2023 AFC Wild Card round, Stroud threw for 274 yards and three touchdowns as Houston demolished Cleveland 45-14, with the Texans turning two Joe Flacco interceptions into defensive touchdowns. In addition to Watson’s health, other storylines include the Texans’ pass rush against Cleveland’s quarterback protection particularly after Sanders was sacked five times in New Orleans and Houston just recorded eight sacks against the Chargers. home.headline: Saints rookie WR Jordyn Tyson plans to make debut vs. Browns after missing first 7 games with hamstring injury: report
home.blurb: Saints head coach Kellen Moore told reporters that Tyson’s foot slipped out from under him as he was hit from behind. Moore clarified that the issue wasn’t related to the receiver’s injury track record. “Any player in that situation probably has the same diagnosis coming out of this.” Tyson began his college career at Colorado, where he teased his tantalizing potential by averaging 21.4 yards per reception and housing a punt return as a freshman in 2022. In 2024, Tyson broke out with the Sun Devils, helping them reach the College Football Playoff and finished with 75 catches, 1,101 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. Even during a shortened 2025 campaign, he totaled nine TDs, with one of them arriving on the ground. The delayed debut of New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is reportedly right around the corner. Tyson, this year’s No. 8 overall pick who missed the Saints’ first seven games with a right hamstring injury, plans to play Sunday against the Cleveland Browns, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . The former Arizona State standout “should be good to go,” Schultz reported Saturday. Tyson’s latest hamstring setback occurred in August during a training camp practice. He left that joint session with the Jacksonville Jaguars early once his run after the catch ended with an awkward fall near the sideline . “I think my understanding of this one, any player that was put in his situation where your foot slips and you get shoved from behind, this has nothing to do with Jordyn's history,” Moore said at the time, per ESPN . Notably, Tyson missed four games last season at Arizona State with multiple hamstring problems, and his injury obstacles affected his pre-draft process. Still, the Saints selected him in the top 10 . Funny enough, that special teams score came against his future school, Arizona State, on a day when he also reeled in five passes for 115 yards and another TD. Staying on the field has been a challenge for the 6-foot-2, 203-pound Tyson. Down the stretch of his lone go-around at Colorado, he suffered a torn ACL, MCL and PCL. He missed the end of a memorable 2024 season with the Sun Devils due to a broken collarbone that sidelined him for the Big 12 title game and the CFP. But he’s thought to have WR1 upside, given his ball skills — including his knack for making contested catches — and his ability to play every receiver spot on the field with impressive quickness. At the moment, the 2-5 Saints are tied for third in the league with 39 pass attempts per game . Without a reliable run game, Tyler Shough is having to chuck the ball around the yard. Having Tyson at his disposal should help.

home.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
home.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. But thanks to Deshaun Watson landing in concussion protocol, there is some uncertainty at the quarterback position for this upcoming game against the New Orleans Saints . Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. Shedeur Sanders announced as Week 9 starter for Browns "Browns Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback vs. the Saints, Todd Monken announced," Cabot reports. This is some major news for the Browns, though it isn't a huge surprise, as a player clearing concussion protocol in the same week they were put on it doesn't happen very often. Sanders will now get a prime opportunity to prove himself worthy of being the starting quarterback this season. Considering Watson hasn't exactly been playing at a super high level, Sanders could make a real case to keep the starting job in Week 9. He will go up against a very leaky Saints defense that has allowed plenty of teams to put up very big offensive days. picks.blurb: Kirk Cousins Trade Creates Massive Shift in Vikings vs. Packers Odds for NFL Week 10 Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Minnesota Vikings made the biggest splash in the NFL ahead of the trade deadline, acquiring veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a third-round pick. With former No. 1 overall pick Kyler Murray set to miss more than just Week 9 with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, the Vikings were desperate to upgrade at quarterback after falling to 6-2. Carson Wentz was awful on Monday night in a loss to the Buffalo Bills, and the Vikings couldn't afford to waste an all-time season from their defense. Cousins' acquisition impacted the Vikings' odds across the betting market. Minnesota went from +2400 to +2200 to win the Super Bowl this season at DraftKings Sportsbook , and it also jumped to -250 to make the playoffs. That's significant, as the Vikings have better playoff odds than the Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks in the NFC. Now, with Cousins likely in line to play against Green Bay in Week 10, the Vikings are also gaining some ground in the odds for that matchup. Following Monday's loss to Buffalo, DraftKings Sportsbook had moved the Vikings to 4.5-point underdogs on the road after they opened as three-point underdogs on Sunday night. The Packers have won five of their last six games, so this was always going to be a tough matchup on the road, even though the Vikings beat Green Bay in Week 1. Now, with Cousins in the fold, the line has shifted down to Vikings +3.5 at the best betting sites . That's interesting since DraftKings is reporting that just 20 percent of the moneyline bets and 34 percent of the spread bets in this game are on the Vikings. Clearly, Cousins is viewed as a massive upgrade at quarterback for a Vikings team that enters Week 10 at No. 31 in the league in EPA/Play and No. 30 in success rate. Only the Los Angeles Chargers -- who have yet to win a game this season -- have a worse EPA/Play on offense. It's pretty shocking that the Vikings are 6-2, and they're hoping Cousins can make a quick adjustment to play in Week 10. After all, Cousins spent multiple seasons in Minnesota and has ran an offense very similar to the Vikings' current scheme at previous stops in his career. That should make it easier for him to start on a short week. This season, Cousins had led the Raiders to a 4-5 start, throwing for 2,340 yards, 20 scores and eight picks. He's not nearly as mobile as he was earlier in his career, but Cousins is certainly an upgrade over Wentz, who was unable to move the Vikings' offense in the loss to Buffalo. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Christopher Gates · SB Nation Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:13 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division's basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don't like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday's game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that's just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don't do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. After that game, they'll have a short(er) week and have to travel on the road to Lambeau Field. Their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, is currently dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play against the Bills. We'll have to see if it heals up by the time they kick off against the Packers, or if it'll be Carson Wentz — their current replacement starter — under center. The only other quarterback in Minnesota is Max Brosmer (53-man roster). Below is the current playoff picture in the NFC: San Francisco 49ers: 7-1 (NFC West) Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (NFC North) New York Giants: 5-2-1 (NFC East) Carolina Panthers: 3-5 (NFC South) Chicago Bears: 7-2 Detroit Lions: 6-2 Green Bay Packers: 6-3 Seattle Seahawks: 5-4 Los Angeles Rams: 5-4 Dallas Cowboys: 4-5 New Orleans Saints: 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 3-6 Atlanta Falcons: 3-6 Arizona Cardinals: 3-6 Washington Commanders: 2-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles: 2-7 The Packers are holding onto the seventh seed right now, where they've been for weeks, but the NFC North keeps winning — as do the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, the teams trying to hunt them down from behind. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

away.headline: Exclusive: Kirk Cousins cuts $240K from Georgia mansion’s asking price as he returns to the Minnesota Vikings
away.blurb: NFL quarterback Kirk Cousins has found his way back to the Minnesota Vikings following the Las Vegas Raiders trade—and he's eager to offload his Georgia home as he prepares to make the move. The trade moved Cousins, 38, his wife, Julie Hampton , and their two kids back to the Land of 10,000 Lakes and allowed the Raiders to acquire Fernando Mendoza as their starting quarterback. Following the news, Cousins posted, "Thank you Raiders Nation! Go get em @fernandomendoza." Cousins spent six seasons with the Minnesota Vikings before being traded to the Atlanta Falcons in 2024. While there, he picked up a sprawling $3 million Georgia mansion. The move to Georgia was an emotional one for the Cousins' family, especially for the athlete's wife, who posted a heartfelt goodbye to Minnesota. "We came to Minnesota 6 years ago when Cooper was just 6 month old and Turner came shortly after!! Time flies when you’re having fun! I just want to say thank you to everyone who helped us build our life in Minnesota over the past 6 years. We have the most beautiful memories we will cherish forever!" she penned alongside a slew of images of the family. Then, in April 2026, Cousins was traded to the Las Vegas Raiders. Two days before the news was announced, the NFL pro put his Atlanta property on the market for $2.99 million. Then, in September, Cousins lowered that asking price to $2.75 million. Now, although the family is looking forward to returning to Minnesota, it appears they are still grappling with a real estate headache in the form of their Georgia home. The sprawling abode, which was built in 2004, underwent a dramatic overhaul in 2024, likely in anticipation of Cousins and his family moving in. The listing described it as offering "timeless architecture enhanced with sophisticated, modern finishes throughout." It is located in a gated community known as The River Club, where many Falcons players choose to live because of its impressive communal amenities, top-of-the-line security, and, of course, its enormous mansions. Cousins' dwelling spans more than 10,000 square feet on a 0.9-acre lot and features six bedrooms and 6.5 bathrooms, providing more than enough room for the quarterback and his family. Enormous trees shield the home from its neighbors, ensuring maximum privacy, while a huge front porch provides the perfect place to relax away from the glaring heat of the Georgia sunshine. Inside, the home features a very traditional aesthetic, starting with an elegant entryway that leads to a soaring double-height great room, complete with a large stone fireplace and patio doors that open to the backyard. The ground floor is filled with open entertaining spaces, including a formal dining room and a huge "designer kitchen" with a large island and a separate breakfast nook. away.headline: Vikings-Bills Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. Green Bay also ruled out five: linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee). Both Nixon and Lloyd popped up on the injury report during the practice week. Nixon didn't practice Thursday but returned in limited fashion Friday. He's played in 76 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. While Rhyan was ruled out, LaFleur told reporters on Thursday that he doesn't anticipate Green Bay's starting center going on IR. picks.blurb: What to know as Vanderbilt says recovery from hack may take weeks News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Jacksonville Jaguars, matchups, prediction NFL Week 10 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Nov. 11, 2026, 5:02 a.m. CT With a 1-7 record, the Titans' focus for the rest of the season is on player evaluation. The Jacksonville Jaguars lead the AFC South and have strengthened their defense with recent trades. Trading Jeffery Simmons changed everything. The Tennessee Titans quietly submitted to a lost 2026 NFL season by dealing their eighth-year All-Pro defensive tackle to the Chicago Bears on Oct. 29. Tennessee general manager Mike Borgonzi then reinforced the team's desire to build for the future by trading eighth-year veteran safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 10. Barring a miraculous playoff push without their top two defenders, rivalry points seem to be all that matter for the Titans (1-7) in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at Nissan Stadium on Nov. 15 (noon CT, FOX). The Titans’ final nine-game stretch will be about observations. Will quarterback Cam Ward play more like a franchise quarterback to finish his second season? Will star rookies Carnell Tate and Anthony Hill Jr. maintain their pace? Who are becoming pieces for Borgonzi’s long-term vision? Finding a way to win one-score games — the Titans have lost six — can help answer those questions regardless of the team’s final record. The Jaguars have won five of their past six games and have a three-game lead in the AFC South. They enhanced their defense this week by trading for All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and 10th-year defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Jaguars. One Jacksonville Jaguars stat to know: 28 That’s career interceptions for Bates. He’ll be a factor. He has at least one interception in each of his nine NFL seasons. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Jaguars Is Ward really the Titans’ only hope? He takes a lot of criticism, some deserved. But why can’t he be an advantage this time? He played at an elite level with a career-high 304 yards passing and two TDs against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. A Ward hot streak in November may be Tennessee’s best chance. The Jaguars rank 21st in the league in passing yards allowed per game (229.0). That’s one spot lower than Cincinnati. There’s an opportunity for Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll to give Ward more downfield throws as he did against the Bengals. Where Jacksonville Jaguars have edge vs. Titans Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence could have a big day against the Titans’ secondary, which was already leaky and now lacks its best player in Hooker. Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals shredded Tennessee with 462 yards passing, three touchdowns and nine plays of 18 yards or more. He was intercepted three times, but all of those came from Hooker. Aside from Alontae Taylor's solid debut at nickel cornerback against the Bengals, other parts of the secondary displayed poor tackling and bad angles. Tennessee ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed (258.3). Lawrence has thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions. He's first in the league with 8.6 yards per pass among active quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Jaguars receiver Parker Washington has 493 yards on 29 catches and is ninth among league receivers with five touchdowns. He ranks third at 17 yards per catch. Matchup to watch Titans defensive end Jacob Martin versus Jaguars left tackle Walker Little. Martin is Tennessee’s best pass rusher with Simmons gone. He had three sacks against the Bengals and has 6.5 for the season. The Jaguars have shuffled their left tackle spot this season. Little has made only three starts, but he didn’t allow a single pressure or sack in last week’s 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Score prediction: Jaguars 28, Titans 21 Ward and the Titans' offense will maintain their recent progress. But Tennessee's inability to finish games will also continue. picks.blurb: Early Jaguars odds vs. the Titans and a bold Jessie Bates III prediction Skip to main content News FanSided NFL Sites With the trade deadline taking the spotlight , it's easy to forget that the Jacksonville Jaguars will face off against the rival Tennessee Titans in Week 10. They should feel good about their odds of coming out on top. Leaving aside that general manager James Gladstone traded for defensive tackle Davon Godchaux, defensive tackle Jordan Davis, and safety Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville enjoyed a long break after trouncing the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night . This doesn't mean that the Jags can start uncorking the champagne just yet, but they'll most definitely have several things going in their favor, even though the game will take place in Nashville. With this in mind, here are the early odds and a bold prediction about the newly acquired Bates for this upcoming AFC South showdown. The Jaguars vs. the Titans odds for Week 10 The Jaguars are a 10.5-point road favorite in Week 10 with a moneyline of -600. Place a wager of $600 and win $100 for a total payout of $700 if they beat Tennessee. The Titans' moneyline sits at +440. Bet $100 on them and win $100 for a total payout of $540 if they defeat Jacksonville. The over/under is set at 46.5 points. ** Odds are refreshed periodically, so they're subjected to change at any moment. You may also like: Updated depth chart after the Jaguars' masterclass at the trade deadline Jessie Bates III bold prediction for the Jaguars vs. the Titans in Week 10 The Jacksonville Jaguars began the eve of the trade deadline with a bang, sending a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons in return for Jessie Bates III. The only reason the trade didn't garner more attention is that Jacksonville eventually acquired defensive tackle Jordan Davis. Anyway, not only will Bates help fill the void left by Eric Murray's season-ending injury but will give the secondary a massive boost as well. A second-round pick of the Cincinnati Bengals in 2018, the former Wake Forest Demon Deacon is a ballhawk who's made the Pro Bowl and earned three Second-Team All-Pro designations. Simply put, he'll bring a big-play element at safety. General manager James Gladstone said as much after the trade deadline. "Yeah, I think a big piece to it, and I know it's one you've heard before, is tying our rush and coverage together, and how important that is, and capping rushes with sacks," Gladstone told the local media (14:43 mark) . "I think what Jesse's able to do in coverage is certainly notable. As I mentioned, that stop the run is really the number one element to our defensive identity. Well, limiting explosives is number two, and creating takeaways is number three." Gladstone continued, "Jesse is extremely good and secure when it comes to being the last line of defense, and really not allowing stuff to slip out and minimizing the opportunities for run after catch and even stuff getting over your head, while at the same time being able to take the ball away at a high clip, whether it's forcing fumbles or creating interceptions. And so I think that element of being a deterrent on the back end will certainly tie in to what our rush can do." Bates will probably go through an onboarding period as he gets acclimated to the Jacksonville defense but will likely get substantial playing time against Tennessee. That, in turn, will allow him to showcase his playmaking skills and result in an interception and a forced fumble. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. Tennessee had an open roster spot after training Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills and decided to poach linebacker Mohamoud Diabate from the Carolina Panthers ' practice squad, adding him to the Titans' active 53-man roster. home.blurb: Bills acquire playmaking safety Amani Hooker from Titans, send second-round pick in return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL The Bills announced at Tuesday's NFL trade deadline that they are sending the Titans a 2027 second-round draft pick and will also receive a 2027 fifth-round selection in return to acquire Hooker. The Bills also inquired about eight-time Pro Bowl Cardinals safety Budda Baker before trading for Hooker, NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports . Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers Jason Owens Staff writer Tue, November 10, 2026 at 9:04 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads With their sights set on a Super Bowl title, the Buffalo Bills are adding a dynamic defensive playmaker in trading for Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker. The move bolsters a defense that ranks 29th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game. The Bills have one of the league's best offenses helmed by an MVP quarterback in Josh Allen, but their pass defense has been a liability throughout the season. Trading a second-round pick to acquire Hooker is a steep price, but the move addresses a clear area of need for a Super Bowl contender. Hooker, 28, is a difference-maker in the secondary. He joins the Bills tied for the league lead with five interceptions alongside six passes defended. The interception tally also ties a career high through just seven games. Hooker has 17 interceptions and 45 passes defended in his career. Hooker is also an accomplished defender against the run. He ranks second on the Titans this season with 52 total tackles. He projects to plug in as an immediate starter for the Bills. An eighth-year veteran, Hooker has played his entire NFL career for the Titans since they selected him in the fourth round of the 2019 draft. For the Titans, they part with a long-term veteran leader and one of their best players. But Hooker is best suited to contribute to a team ready to win now, and at 1-7, the Titans are not that. A second-round pick is a valuable asset as they seek to continue to rebuild around second-year quarterback Cam Ward.

home.headline: Amani Hooker Traded to Bills, Titans' NFL Draft Pick Return Revealed After Deadline Deal
home.blurb: The Buffalo Bills bolstered their defense ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. Buffalo acquired safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick from the Tennessee Titans in exchange for a second-round draft pick. The Ringer's Tom Pelissero and ESPN's Adam Schefter first reported the deal. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that prior to dealing for Hooker, the Bills "made a very strong push" for Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker. A 2019 fourth-round pick, Hooker had spent his entire career in Tennessee. His fellow draft classmate Jeffery Simmons was also shipped away this season, with the Titans sending the standout defensive tackle to the Chicago Bears. Hooker is tied for the league lead with five interceptions this year, giving him 17 picks for his career. He's also added 52 total tackles and six passes defended this season. Hooker is an immediate upgrade for the Bills, who have a combined total of six interceptions through eight games. Buffalo added veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson over the offseason, but his disappointing tenure included a one-game suspension and subpar play before he was released earlier this month. If Hooker lives up to expectations, he could be the missing piece that puts the team over the top as title contenders. The Bills already appear to be the favorites to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, improving to 7-1 with a 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football .
