away.blurb: After he was aquired, McCord said of his strengths: "Knowing the call and then seeing what the defense plays and getting the ball to the right guy on time, allowing the playmakers to go out and make plays. Miami would like Willis to at least be their starting quarterback for two seasons. But nothing in life is guaranteed, especially for NFL quarterbacks. McCord, 24, played at Ohio State and Syracuse and was a 6th round pick of the Eagles. On trading deadline day, the Dolphins did not make a deal. away.headline: Who is Kyle McCord? Meet the Miami Dolphins Week 10 starting quarterback
away.source: Last Word On Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Kyle McCord is no stranger to the limelight, even in high school. Coming out of St. Joseph’s Prep, one of the best high school football programs in Pennsylvania, McCord was rated a 4-star recruit as the 49th-ranked player in the country. He was ranked third in PA behind fellow St. Joseph Hawk Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and also shared the top 10 with his lead target, Marvin Harrison Jr. Talk about a crazy high school Big 3. McCord and company went 6-0 in his senior 2020 campaign, finishing the season with a 3rd straight state championship (he started 2 of the 3) and a #4 national ranking. After getting limited appearances during his freshman and sophomore seasons, McCord finally got the opportunity he’d been waiting for and became the Buckeyes’ starting quarterback for his 2023 junior season. For the most part, McCord did a decent job as Ohio State’s signal caller, throwing for 3170 passing yards with a 65.8 completion percentage, 24 touchdowns, 6 interceptions, and leading OSU to an 11-0 start to the season. Unfortunately, 2 of those interceptions came in 2023’s installment of “The Game,” with Ohio State falling to the Michigan Wolverines 30-24, which capped off McCord’s time in the Scarlet and Gray. Since the College Football Playoff hadn’t gone crazy with expansion just yet, the #6-ranked Buckeyes were out of the playoff, leading to McCord opting out of their eventual 14-3 loss to Missouri in the Cotton Bowl. McCord wasn’t even a Buckeye at that point, as he had already become a member of the Syracuse Orange 12 days prior. It’s still unclear as to how McCord is going to play as an NFL quarterback, considering this will be his first regular-season snaps, let alone his first start. He could opt to continue his gunslinging ways from college, or instead want to slowly ease into the role by looking for shorter passes more akin to his preseason play. He is a complete wild card in terms of how he’ll play, which, for a team like Miami that is perfectly fine with trying something out to see what will stick for the future, is at the very least intriguing. It is encouraging, however, that he threw most of his preseason passes in the intermediate middle of the field with good precision. On the bright side, McCord will not be completely hung out to dry. Running back and fellow 2025 6th-round pick Ollie Gordon has been incredibly productive since stepping into the starting role in place of the injured De’Von Achane, so McCord should at least have a good running game to fall back on. Kadyn Proctor’s return to the starting lineup last week also gives a stout blindside with him and tackle Patrick Paul to pair with All-Pro center Aaron Brewer. The less said about the right side of the line, however, the better. Hopefully, they’ll pick it up for their young QB. Dolphins Lose Malik Willis for at Least Four Weeks in Major Injury Blow The Miami Dolphins have suffered another significant setback in what has already been a challenging 2026 season. Quarterback Malik Willis is being placed on injured reserve after an MRI revealed that the groin injury he has been battling has developed into a core muscle injury. According to the report, Willis will miss at least four weeks, although the injury is not considered season-ending. The news is another major blow to a Dolphins offense that has struggled to find consistency throughout the season. Willis' Mobility Has Been Compromised One of the biggest reasons the Dolphins brought Willis to Miami was his ability to make plays with his legs and extend plays outside the pocket. Willis has continued playing through the injury, but his reduced mobility has made it more difficult for him to escape pressure, create opportunities outside the pocket, and threaten opposing defenses as a runner. For a quarterback whose athleticism is such an important part of his skill set, that limitation is significant. Now, with the injury developing into a core muscle issue, the Dolphins have decided that Willis needs time to recover rather than continuing to play through the discomfort. Kyle McCord Could Get His Opportunity With Willis heading to injured reserve, the Dolphins face an important decision at quarterback. Kyle McCord, whom Miami acquired from the Green Bay Packers earlier this season, could now have an opportunity to show what he can do in meaningful regular-season action. McCord offers a different style of quarterback play than Willis. While Willis is known for his athleticism and ability to create plays on the move, McCord is more of a traditional pocket passer who relies on timing, accuracy, and decision-making. For head coach Jeff Hafley and offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik, this could provide an opportunity to evaluate how the offense functions with a different quarterback under center. It could also give Miami valuable information about McCord's potential role in the team's future. The Dolphins are placing QB Malik Willis on injured reserve, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports. Westbrook-Ikhine, 6-2, 211 pounds, has played in three games this season. He was signed to the team's practice squad on August 31, 2026. Westbrook-Ikhine participated in Indianapolis' 2026 offseason program and training camp after originally being signed by the team as a free agent March 18, 2026. He has played in 96 career games (42 starts) in his time with the Colts (2026), Miami Dolphins (2025) and Tennessee Titans (2020-24). Westbrook-Ikhine has totaled 137 receptions for 1,862 yards (13.6 avg.) and 19 touchdowns. away.headline: Carolina Panthers vs. Broncos: Who will win? Predictions, injury report, TV info
away.blurb: Out: CB Will Lee (hamstring), G Damien Lewis (knee), LB Bobby Okereke (foot), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), OL Brady Christensen (hamstring)* Questionable: OL Corey Bullock (quad), OL Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) Out: CB Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle), S Brandon Jones (hamstring), DL Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder) Questionable: WR Pat Bryant (ankle), OLB Dondrea Tilman (hip), S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) Alex Zietlow: Broncos 31, Panthers 21. The Panthers will be experimenting a bunch this week. They’ll presumably shake the personnel up along the offensive line, and they’ll have a new defensive coach calling plays. Such risks might work out for them, kind of like how their RPOs stunned the Lions’ defense on Sunday Night Football (gosh, that feels like a lifetime ago!). Even still, I think the Broncos are too talented on defense and too disciplined on offense to let a winnable game like this slip away. Sunday, they’ll want to steady the ship. And they will have to pull off an upset to do so. The Panthers (3-4) still sit atop the NFC South, but in order to hold onto their station, they’ll likely need to emerge from Bank of America Stadium with a victory against one of the powers of the AFC — the Denver Broncos (6-2). The Sean Payton-led team has won its last four contests, including a 28-24 thriller against the Chiefs. Another flattering Broncos stat: They’re 15-0 in their last 15 regular-season one-score games . Here’s a one-stop shop for everything you need to know ahead of the contest, including score predictions, betting odds, injury statuses and more. TV, radio information for Panthers-Packers The Panthers’ Week 9 matchup will begin at 1 p.m. Sunday in uptown Charlotte’s largest venue. It’ll be broadcast on CBS; Ian Eagle will do the play-by-play, with Ross Tucker as the analyst and Evan Washburn as the sideline reporter. Fans can also catch the game on the radio: WRFX The Fox: 99.7 FM. Anish Shroff (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (analyst), Jake Delhomme (analyst), Jim Szoke (host), Kristen Balboni (sideline reporter). Check the Panthers Radio Network for full listings. Spanish Radio: WXNC 97.3 FM, 1060 AM. Jaime Moreno (play-by-play), Antonio Ramos (analyst). Betting odds for Carolina-Denver game The Panthers are 2.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook on Sunday morning . The over/under for the contest is 44.5 points. The Panthers are 3-4 against the spread so far this season. The Broncos are 6-2. Broncos head coach Sean Payton has a long history in the NFC South. That included a Super Bowl in New Orleans. Payton’s record against the Panthers, according to Pro Football Reference, is 19-13, including the only win as Broncos head coach against the Panthers in 2024. Some more connections between the programs: Ejiro Evero had a successful stint as defensive coordinator in Denver prior to coming over to Carolina; Evero was fired from the Panthers last week; Sunday will mark Todd Wash’s debut as interim defensive coordinator and play caller. home.headline: Saints' roster moves may suggest good news for Travis Etienne Jr.
home.blurb: Smartt played for Kellen Moore on the Philadelphia Eagles but wasn't called up for a game after reuniting in New Orleans. He suffered an injury at practice and will be sidelined, but that means the team can open a spot on the practice squad until he's able to return. Welch has been a consistent part of the offense as a blocking tight end in five of the first eight games, and the Saints obviously want to keep him around. He also has been on the field for 47 snaps on special teams, mostly with the kick return and punt coverage units. The latest New Orleans Saints roster moves could signal good news for Travis Etienne Jr. Last week, we saw the Saints release a wide receiver from their practice squad just before activating first-round pick Jordyn Tyson from injured reserve. Etienne is eligible to come off of injured reserve, too, and the Saints just let one of their practice squad running backs go. Those are some easy dots to connect, but nothing is official until the team says so. For now, here's what you need to know about each of the Saints' recent roster moves going into Week 10's game with the Carolina Panthers : RB Jarquez Hunter released from the practice squad Hunter was signed after injuries hit the position hard, landing Etienne on injured reserve and sidelining CJ Donaldson for multiple weeks. He never got into a game while Zamir White was called up for Week 9's overtime win over the Carolina Panthers. Moving on from Hunter now seems to suggest Etienne will be back soon, leaving fewer snaps to go around at practice. Good luck to him in his next opportunity. TE Stone Smartt placed on practice squad IR TE Treyton Welch re-signed to the practice squad TE Matt Lauter signed to the practice squad Here's a new face. Lauter played college football at Boise State and signed with the Las Vegas Raiders as a rookie free agent, but ended up with the Minnesota Vikings by the end of the preseason. He's an experienced run blocker (1,175 snaps in that role in college) with some receiving ability (nine touchdown catches in his last two years). Let's see what he's got. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They kept it competitve for a half. In the first half the Jets outgained the Chiefs. They won the turnover battle. They had more than twice the time of possession as the Chiefs. They scored on four out of five possessions. The Chiefs scored only twice. And still the Jets trailed at halftime, 14 – 12. It was an ill omen. The second half was all Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 – 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Bills are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Recent history adds another challenge for New York. Buffalo has won eight of the past 10 meetings, including a couple smacks last season, beating the Jets 30-10 at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 14, 2025 and 35-8 in Buffalo on Jan. 4, 2026. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. home.headline: What Jets Are Saying About Week 9 Injury Report Ahead of Sunday
home.blurb: The good news is that edge rusher David Bailey and running back Breece Hall are both expected to play. Bailey missed Week 8 with a groin injury while a quad injury kept Hall out for the last five. Even better, the team could have their full collection of edge rushers with Joseph Ossai potentially back as well. But with every piece of good news there is also bad. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson has been ruled out for Sunday's contest with a concussion. He reported the injury on Monday and has been in protocol ever since. His absence, coupled with the return of some key veterans, have Jets players and coaches talking about their chances in Week 9 against Kansas City. Here's the full injury report from the Jets' practice on Friday with three clear distinctions on who is out for Sunday: Of note, the three players that are out extend beyond Wilson. Special teamer Trevin Wallace is also out while Ossai, rookie safety VJ Payne, defensive tackle Harrison Phillips, and corner Nahshon Wright are all listed as questionable. The same can be said for the second-overall pick in Bailey. His return gives the team more flexibility to rush the passer—even one as elite as Patrick Mahomes. "He (Bailey) just has to understand that with Mahomes is going to fake throw," Glenn said. "He's going to move around, and we just got to make sure we squeeze the pocket and make sure we don't let him out of the pocket in situations like that." What Jets Are Saying About Week 9 Injury Report Ahead of Sunday Skip to main content SI.COM There is good news and bad news when it comes to the New York Jets injury report heading into Week 9 against the Kansas City Chiefs. Friday’s injury report for #NYJvsKC pic.twitter.com/S8vga27YX3 The good news is Mason Taylor, Hall, and Bailey are all starters and will need to be on the field for the Jets to have any chance against the Chiefs. Speaking to reporters before practice on Friday, Glenn was clear: the team was prepared to play without Wilson, but that doesn't mean his absence will be anything less than a major blow to the entire unit. "I think it speaks for itself," Glenn said. "Any time you lose a player of that magnitude, it's always tough, right, but we do have other players, and those guys will look forward to the challenge." Glenn did acknowledge the benefit that came from having Hall back in the lineup . He made it clear that the former second-round running back was going to have a role in the offense on Sunday, and it will be to work with rising star Braelon Allen. "I know we're trying to get in this who's going to be the starter and try to spin sort of a negative situation, but nothing's changed from how I see this," Glenn said. "Both of those guys will play and that's just what it is." It's hard to envision a Jets victory on Sunday without Wilson. But getting several starters back healthy will certainly help. picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 predictions: Jaxon Smith-Njigba First TD odds as Klint Kubiak faces his old offense - oregonlive.com Skip to Article Set weather Back To Main Menu Close Weather in - Change Location Current - Mostly Sunny Tonight Low - Mostly Sunny Tomorrow High - Mostly Sunny Full Weather Report Sports Betting Published: Nov. 11, 2026, 9:15 a.m. Sina Torki | Special Correspondent Klint Kubiak called the plays for Seattle’s Super Bowl offense last season. On Sunday he sees that offense from the other sideline. Kubiak’s Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) host the Seahawks (5-4) at Allegiant Stadium, and the betting market has spent the week moving toward his team. DraftKings opened Seattle as a 7-point favorite, according to ESPN . Bet365 now has the Seahawks at -3.5. Seattle comes in off a 17-3 home win over Arizona. Las Vegas lost 38-17 at San Francisco. The records and recent form favor the Seahawks, but the line movement says the market thinks this is much closer to a field-goal game than it first looked. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is again the shortest price to score first, though at a longer number than he was against the Cardinals. Teams: Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders Date: Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026 Kickoff: 1:05 p.m. PT (4:05 p.m. ET) Location: Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas TV: CBS ( Seahawks viewing guide ) Records: Seahawks 5-4, Raiders 4-5 More: NFL.com game center · NFL standings · NFL injury reports Seahawks vs. Raiders odds Odds are from Bet365 and are accurate at time of publication. Spread: Seahawks -3.5 (-105), Raiders +3.5 (-115) Moneyline: Seahawks -182, Raiders +152 Total: Over 43.5 (-105), Under 43.5 (-115) The moneyline implies roughly 64.5% for Seattle. The spread and total together point to a final around Seahawks 23.5, Raiders 20. Las Vegas is the more expensive side of the spread at -115, a sign the market still sees value in the hook even after three and a half points of movement. Jaxon Smith-Njigba to score the first touchdown (+425) Bet365 has Smith-Njigba at +425 to open the scoring , an implied probability of roughly 19.0%. His -130 anytime price implies roughly 56.5%. He was +350 to score first against Arizona last week, so the market has lengthened him in a game it expects to be closer and played on the road. He leads Seattle with 1,036 receiving yards and nine touchdowns, per NFL.com , and is the only player on this board priced shorter than even money to score at any point. The gap to the rest of the board is narrower than last week. Zach Charbonnet is +600 to score first (roughly 14.3%) and Brock Bowers is +625 (roughly 13.8%), both about five points behind. On the anytime market, Charbonnet and Bowers are both +115 (roughly 46.5%), 10 points back. Bowers is the case against. The Raiders score 26.4 points per game, eighth in the league, four more than Seattle’s 22.4. Kirk Cousins has 20 touchdown passes, and Bowers has six touchdown catches as his top target. The board makes Seattle more likely to score first, with the visible Seahawks (Smith-Njigba, Charbonnet and Jadarian Price) at roughly 44.4% against 33.2% for the visible Raiders (Bowers, Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr.), before the sportsbook’s margin. But Las Vegas has been the better scoring team this season, and Bowers at +625 gets you most of Smith-Njigba’s chance at a better price. If you think Kubiak’s knowledge of Seattle’s defense gives the Raiders an edge early, Bowers is the alternative to Smith-Njigba. First and anytime touchdown scorer odds Jaxon Smith-Njigba Zach Charbonnet Jadarian Price Ashton Jeanty Mike Washington Jr. Jeanty’s +800 is long for a back drafted sixth overall a year ago. NFL.com lists him at 362 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown this season, which goes a long way toward explaining the price. Washington’s presence on the board points to a Las Vegas backfield that is more of a split than Jeanty’s draft position suggested. Kirk Cousins passing yards Bet365’s passing yardage ladder has Cousins at -165 to reach 225 yards (roughly 62.3%) and +115 to reach 250 (roughly 46.5%). His last five games came in at 243, 313, 295, 247 and 216. He cleared 225 in four of them and 250 in two. Las Vegas ranks 30th in time of possession, so its drives tend to be short and pass-heavy, and that supports the 225 line. Same Game Parlays on the board Bet365’s featured Same Game Parlays for this game: Four Score (+1900, $10 pays $200): Zach Charbonnet, Ashton Jeanty, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Brock Bowers each to score a TD End Zone Encore (+2800, $10 pays $290): Jadarian Price, Mike Washington Jr. and Cooper Kupp each to score a TD Four Score takes the top two names from each side and needs a game with plenty of touchdowns, which sits awkwardly with a 43.5 total. End Zone Encore is the long-shot version built from secondary options. Kupp doesn’t appear among the six visible names on the touchdown scorer board. Seahawks vs. Raiders prediction and best bet A spread that moves from 7 to 3.5 usually means one of two things: new injury information or a market that decided the opener was wrong. Either way, the value on the Raiders side has mostly been taken. At +3.5 for -115, Las Vegas needs to cover about 53.5% of the time, and it has gone 1-4 in its last five. The total looks more interesting. The market has 43.5 points, and the Under is the more expensive side. The season numbers point the other way. Las Vegas averages 26.4 points and Seattle 22.4, and Cousins has passed for more than 240 yards in four of his last five games. The Raiders rank 30th in time of possession, so their drives are short, which tends to give both offenses more possessions. Kubiak also knows Seattle’s personnel from last season, and that should help Las Vegas’s offense more than its defense. The counterargument is Seattle’s defense, which ranks fourth in interceptions, and a Seahawks offense that sits 17th in yards per game. away.headline: ‘They Didn’t Have To Tell Us That,’ ‘Definitely Unusual’ — NFL Analyst Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Reveal Sam Darnold’s Surprise Injury
away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, but the timing of the team’s announcement seems questionable to some, especially given its decision to disclose the quarterback’s injuries. “So they got a lot of faith in Drew Lock. I just think that this idea that Wednesday, out of the blue, they tell us that Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury. They tell us that he’s week to week, which usually means you’re going to miss a couple of weeks. They didn’t have to tell us that,” Florio said. “Now I appreciate the transparency, because what they could have done, they could have just put him down as did not practice. They could have done that yesterday. They could have done it today. They could have done it tomorrow, and then they could have called him out on Friday,” the analyst continued. Drew Lock is expected to start against Arizona, although his availability for Seattle is not settled. The veteran is managing a right-elbow injury and was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated injury report after Seattle held a walkthrough. Darnold, meanwhile, is considered week-to-week and has not been placed on injured reserve. The cracked rib could potentially be managed while playing, but the quad injury is expected to keep him out against Arizona. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Wednesday that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game because of a quad injury suffered late in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mike Florio Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Announce Sam Darnold’s Absence Early While the coach disclosed the injury, Macdonald also revealed that the quarterback had played through a cracked rib for nearly the entire game. Darnold suffered the injury on the second play against Chicago after taking a hard hit from blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon. He did not report the issue to the coaching or medical staff during the game and continued playing through the final whistle. He finished with two touchdown passes despite the injury, and Seattle’s coaches and medical staff did not learn about the cracked rib until after the game. The decision to reveal the extent of Darnold’s injuries, however, prompted NFL analyst Mike Florio to question why Seattle chose to announce the quarterback’s absence on Wednesday rather than wait until later in the week. Speaking on “NFL on NBC” with Chris Simms, Florio said the Seahawks could have followed the league’s injury reporting rules without immediately confirming that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game. “But they decided to just lead with their chin on this, which I thought was strange. It’s definitely unusual, and it forfeits the uncertainty that the Cardinals would have as to who they’re getting ready for. Now they know they’re getting ready for Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe,” Florio added. away.headline: Seahawks Week 10 national power rankings: Seattle continues to drop despite win over Cardinals
away.blurb: Entering Week 9, the Seattle Seahawks dropped out of the top ten on many power rankings after losing to the Chicago Bears . Will their Week 9 victory over the Arizona Cardinals help raise them back up the rankings? Let’s take a look at five national media sites (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (BR), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where they rank Seattle. ESPN also moved the Seahawks down, albeit only one spot, from eighth to ninth best in the league . In their rankings this week, ESPN noted each teams’ most important game of the second half. For Seattle that was the San Francisco 49ers in week 12. The hope is that the team can get healthy by that week with six starters currently out due to injury. Overall the national landscape remains skeptical over the Seahawks. Not only has the offense been struggling throughout the season, but the team is now flushed with injuries. Currently out of the playoff picture if the season ended today, it makes sense to see Seattle ranked right in the 9-14 range. Entering Week 9, the average power rankings between the five polled sites was 10.2. Entering week 10, that average has continued to fall to 10.6. This next week against the Las Vegas Raiders appears to me a must win for the Seahawks as they enter the bye week and hopefully get healthy for the final stretch of the season. These rankings this week may frustrate some Seahawks fans. Despite the victory over the Cardinals, many national media sites did not move Seattle up. In fact, some even moved the team down their rankings. That being said, let’s start with the one site who did give the Seahawks a positive bump. B/R, who ranked Seattle 13 last week, moved the team up one spot to 12 . In their ranking, B/R expressed some doubts around Seattle’s offense, particularly at the quarterback position that has seen a plethora of injuries in 2026. Because of this, B/R states that “it’s hard to feel confident about the Seahawks’ short-term outlook.” Two national media sites did not move Seattle from their rankings from last week. CBS, who was the lowest on Seattle last week, keeps the team ranked 14th best in the league this week . In this ranking, CBS also brings up the injuries at quarterback, however provides a sliver of hope, stating that “[t]he Raiders might be the perfect tonic to get the offense going.” PFT also kept the Seahawks at the same ranking as last week, that being ninth best in the NFL . PFT also interestingly states that “Drew Lock fits this team better than Sam Darnold does.” The last two national media sites to discuss this week both moved the Seahawks down in their rankings despite the victory. NFL.com is the most punitive, moving the team down two spots, from 7 to 9 . In their reasoning, NFL.com notes that the quarterback situation “might become more concerning in the days ahead” due to the recent injuries to Drew Lock and Sam Darnold. away.headline: Sam Darnold, Drew Lock Injury Updates Provided by Seahawks HC Ahead of Raiders Game
away.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it was the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Meanwhile, backup Drew Lock appeared to get good news as looks to recover from an oblique injury suffered on Sunday: Lock went 19-of-28 for 175 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Darnold has been considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of a Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Lock had been previously been dealing with an elbow injury but played this past week with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (5-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (7-1).

Seahawks QB Sam Darnold ruled out for Week 10 game vs. Raiders; Drew Lock expected to start. https://t.co/lgswpqoeAJ Sam Darnold Injury Update: Latest Return Timeline Darnold's potential return after the bye is the key date for Seahawks supporters. Head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed on Monday that Darnold is still recovering from quad and rib injuries. The decision means Drew Lock is expected to make his second consecutive start, although he is also managing an oblique injury and an elbow issue. Seattle will travel to Las Vegas for the November 15 contest at Allegiant Stadium, with the Seahawks hoping to avoid another quarterback setback before their Week 11 bye. Darnold suffered a quadriceps injury late in Seattle's Week 8 game against the Chicago Bears. He also sustained a cracked rib during the contest, with Macdonald revealing that the quarterback had been playing through the injury. The Seahawks initially described his absence as week to week. Darnold subsequently missed Seattle's 17-3 victory over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. There is some encouragement for Seattle, however. Drew Lock Expected To Start Despite Injuries Lock is set to remain Seattle's starting quarterback, but his own fitness situation is worth watching. He entered the Cardinals game dealing with an elbow problem and picked up an oblique injury during the contest. Despite the issue, Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in the 17-3 win. He also avoided throwing an interception. Macdonald said Lock had a good medical examination and that the oblique injury was manageable. The Seahawks will manage his practice workload during the week rather than expose him to every throwing session. That approach should give Seattle a chance to prepare Lock while keeping rookie Jalen Milroe ready as the backup. Could Jalen Milroe Get His First Opportunity? Milroe remains an important part of the quarterback situation. With both Darnold and Lock dealing with injuries, Seattle cannot afford to overlook its contingency plan. Macdonald indicated that Milroe would continue to receive practice repetitions, including opportunities to handle the full workload. away.blurb: Written by NDTV Sports Desk Updated: November 05, 2026, 7:53 AM EST Read Time: 2 min facebook twitter WhatsApp reddit E-mail Matthew Stafford during an NFL game. © X/@RamsNFL The Los Angeles Rams QB Matthew Stafford walking around with ice wrapped around his throwing elbow raises questions about his health. With the team already dealing with several injuries, losing another player was the last thing they needed. However, Stafford had a rather relaxed response when reporters asked about his condition on Wednesday, November 4. The 38-year-old made it clear that the soreness had not affected his work or his ability to play. Matthew Stafford speaks out on injury concern Stafford did not appear particularly concerned about the attention surrounding his elbow. In fact, he joked that reporters had only recently started noticing something he had been doing throughout the season. "You guys have been blind. I feel like I've been icing my arm every day out here, walking around," the quarterback told reporters. He then explained that some discomfort was understandable at this stage of his career. Stafford, in his 18th NFL season, admitted the physical demands of competing against younger players but insisted that the issue had not stopped him from practicing or taking snaps on game day. "Listen, I'm 38 years old, trying to keep up with these young bucks. Little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year," he added. His comments gave some relief after head coach Sean McVay had confirmed earlier in the week that Stafford was experiencing soreness in his right arm. The quarterback had been spotted with ice on his elbow after the 24-9 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8. The first injury report for Week 9 listed Stafford with a right elbow issue, but he remained a full participant in practice. That was another positive sign for a team relying heavily on its veteran quarterback. Los Angeles Rams face a growing injury list Stafford's update came at a time when the Los Angeles Rams had several other players dealing with injuries. Cornerback Jaylen Watson became the latest major loss after suffering a shoulder injury that required season-ending surgery. He was the third Rams player to suffer a season-ending injury in two weeks. Wide receiver Davante Adams was among those missing from the team's first Week 9 practice report, while cornerback Trent McDuffie was listed with a back injury. Tight end Colby Parkinson remained sidelined with the rib injury that kept him out against the Los Angeles Chargers. Stafford admitted that every NFL season brought its own challenges and said he did not spend time comparing the current situation with previous injury-hit campaigns. He said that players in the training room were working hard to return, adding that their availability would give the team a good welcome . away.headline: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett’s huge injury return is a Los Angeles first since Aaron Donald
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett made an immediate impact in his return, notching three sacks and forcing a fumble during Sunday’s 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. The performance put the 30-year-old in rare company, as he became the first player in franchise history to record three sacks and a forced fumble since star pass rusher Aaron Donald accomplished the feat back in 2020. His first sack came in the second quarter when he knocked the ball out of quarterback Jayden Daniels’ hands. Linebacker Omar Speights recovered the fumble, helping Los Angeles get into position for a field goal that reduced Washington’s advantage to 10-6 before halftime. Garrett added two more sacks in the fourth quarter, including one against Daniels after coming around left tackle Brandon Coleman. His final takedown turned out to be a game-changer, as he beat the replacement center with a quick move through the middle to prevent the Commanders from building momentum during their late comeback attempt. Garrett’s return helped Los Angeles improve to 5-4, extend its winning streak to three games and move above .500 for the first time this season. The Rams will next face the division-rival Arizona Cardinals before entering its Week 11 bye. Garrett, who underwent knee surgery in mid-September after initially attempting to play through the injury, missed seven weeks before returning to action in Week 9. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year wasted little time demonstrating his value, generating six quarterback pressures on 27 pass-rush attempts, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. He also managed a 22.2% pressure rate while playing 35 of the Rams’ 58 defensive snaps. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The three-sack performance was Garrett’s ninth career game with at least three sacks, the most by any player since Hall of Famer DeMarcus Ware in 2014, according to ESPN Research. He also brought his career sack total to 128.5, tying Hall of Famer Jared Allen for the second-most sacks by a player through his first 10 NFL seasons since the statistic became official in 1982. The contest also was the first time Garrett shared the field with Donald , who retired in March 2024. Across 23 plays with both defensive stars on the field, the Rams surrendered just 5.0 yards per play and recorded four sacks. During the other 19 plays, the defense allowed 8.0 yards per play and a touchdown without producing a sack. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. Over the past four weeks, the Cardinals rank a respectable 19th in points per drive allowed and 12th in yards per play allowed. It’s been their best defensive stretch in nearly two years. On the flip side, their offense ranks 24th and 28th, respectively, in those same metrics. “The defense, there's been a guy here and there, but there's been some decent continuity over the last month,” LaFleur said. “And I think you guys see that. I think you see 11 as one more and more each week, particularly over these last four weeks. Not the case on offense right now.” It’s an injury barrage that is unmatched across the league. The Cardinals’ seven offensive players on injured reserve is the most in the league, with those four aforementioned Week 1 starters joined by Gardner Minshew, Jalen Brooks and Hunter Long. Only one other team — the Los Angeles Chargers — even has six offensive players on IR. League average is 2.7. When looking only at offensive starters, the story is similar, as the Cardinals lead the league with four on IR. Only two teams — the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Rams — have three offensive starters on IR. League average is 1.2. The Cardinals’ defense, by contrast, has had slightly better health than league average. Still, just 43 of the 53 players from the Cardinals’ Week 1 squad remain on the active roster. Only the Atlanta Falcons have had more attrition. As a result, it’s difficult to assess exactly where the Cardinals roster stands. That’s not to say that their poor performances have been entirely attributable to injury — Marvin Harrison Jr., the offensive line and the pass rush have all struggled even when healthy. But any overarching assessment, at least on offense, has to account for the unwelcome wave of injuries.

home.headline: Arizona Cardinals face quarterback crisis as Gardner Minshew faces potential season-ending injury
home.blurb: Head coach Mike LaFleur addressed the media on Monday, confirming that Minshew is scheduled for an MRI to determine the full extent of the damage. While the team has not officially ruled the quarterback out for the year, the organization is already preparing for a transition under center. Reports indicate that rookie Carson Beck is the primary candidate to assume the starting responsibilities should Minshew be placed on the sidelines for an extended period. The Arizona Cardinals are confronting a significant roster challenge following reports that starting quarterback Gardner Minshew II has sustained a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing arm. The injury, which occurred during Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks, has raised concerns that the 30-year-old signal-caller may be sidelined for the remainder of the season. The incident took place on the final play of the first half when Minshew was struck while being sacked. Despite the severity of the injury, Minshew returned to the field for the third quarter and completed the game. Following the contest, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that the quarterback is undergoing further medical evaluations, with initial assessments suggesting a recovery period that could span several months. Transition to Rookie Leadership and Roster Adjustments Beck’s path to the starting lineup was cleared earlier this week when the Cardinals traded veteran Jacoby Brissett, effectively elevating the rookie to the backup position. Although Beck has yet to make his regular-season debut, he saw significant action during the preseason Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers, where he completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown. His development was previously hindered by a rib injury, but his recent promotion has increased his involvement in team practices. To bolster the quarterback room, the Cardinals are reportedly moving to sign veteran Josh Johnson from the Cleveland Browns' practice squad. The addition of Johnson provides the team with necessary depth as they navigate the uncertainty surrounding Minshew’s status and prepare for the upcoming stretch of the season. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton At one time…a few decades ago…the 49ers and the Cowboys was the top rivalry in the NFL. In 2026, Sunday’s game between the 49ers (7-1) and the Cowboys (4-5) features one team contending for a Super Bowl and the other simply battling to remain in contention in an underwhelming division. The contrast extends beyond the standings is explained in the numbers: the 49ers are averaging 29.4 points per game while allowing 19.5, compared with 27.3 scored and 26.2 allowed by the Cowboys. San Francisco arrives in Arlington following a convincing 38-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a game the 49ers broke open with a turnover-fueled second half. Brock Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns and also ran for a score, while Christian McCaffrey scored once on the ground and once through the air. San Francisco led 21-10 at halftime before Jaden Dugger returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown on the Raiders’ first offensive play of the third quarter. That started a remarkable half in which the 49ers forced five turnovers. The Niners finished with 414 total yards, including 190 rushing, possessed the ball for more than 38 minutes. Dallas also enters the matchup following a victory, escaping Indianapolis with a 27-23 win over the Colts after trailing 23-20 with less than two minutes remaining. Dak Prescott immediately answered with a 46-yard completion to Ryan Flournoy , and Javonte Williams scored from one yard out with 1:08 remaining to put Dallas ahead for good. The Cowboys piled up 508 yards of offense to Indianapolis’ 271, with Prescott completing 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, CeeDee Lamb exploding for 10 catches and 195 yards and a score, and Williams rushing for 101 yards. But Dallas made life difficult for itself with two turnovers and 14 penalties for 153 yards. This is a rivalry that has produced some of the most memorable postseason games in NFL history, from “The Catch” in the 1981 NFC Championship Game to three consecutive NFC title-game meetings between the clubs following the 1992, 1993 and 1994 seasons. San Francisco currently owns the upper hand, leading the all-time series 21-19-1 and having won the past four meetings, including playoff victories of 23-17 after the 2021 season and 19-12 after the 2022 season. The 49ers followed those wins with a 42-10 rout in 2023 and a 30-24 victory in the most recent meeting on Oct. 27, 2024. away.headline: Another 49ers receiver added to injury report ahead of Week 9 vs. Raiders
away.blurb: SANTA CLARA — The 49ers continued to see several of their players return to the field following the bye week, but there also was a new absence. Christian Kirk , who was limited on Wednesday with a knee injury, did not participate in Thursday's practice. The veteran wideout was on the field for 20 offensive snaps in San Francisco's Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons after being sidelined with a calf injury at the start of training camp. Standout special teams players Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford both were back on the field for a second consecutive practice. The two linebackers’ absences were felt in the 49ers' Week 7 loss to the Falcons, when return coverage was clearly challenged. Christian Kirk added to 49ers injury report before Week 9 game – NBC Sports Bay Area & California Warriors Yet another 49ers receiver was added to the injury report ahead of San Francisco's Week 9 game vs. the Las Vegas Raiders. Demarcus Robinson , however, participated in his second straight practice after missing substantial time with a high ankle sprain. The expectation is that Robinson will be ready for Sunday's game. Nick Bosa was seen on the field for a second consecutive session after missing five games with a calf injury in the leg, and did not suffer the ACL injury in Week 3 of the 2025 season. The All-Pro warmed up alongside DeForest Buckner , who likely will play a sizable role on Sunday. Upton Stout , who has been wearing a blue non-contact jersey, was seen in his standard No. 20 jersey, indicating that he could be healthy enough to play on Sunday. After being sidelined on Wednesday with a hamstring injury, Christian McCaffrey returned to the field, along with Trent Williams , who had a veteran rest day. home.blurb: Jonathan Taylor, Keenan Allen, and Charvarius Ward all returned to full participation after sitting out Wednesday on rest days. None of the three absences appears particularly concerning, and all should be in a good position to play Sunday barring an unexpected setback. Indianapolis could also receive reinforcements at a couple of positions. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher and wide receiver Anthony Gould have both logged consecutive full practices after missing the previous two games. Gould is still required to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before returning to game action, but his progress is an encouraging sign. Boettcher's potential return would be particularly helpful for a linebacker group dealing with some uncertainty. Tight end Drew Ogletree also showed some progress, moving from a DNP designation Wednesday to limited participation Thursday. His availability remains unclear, but the progression is a positive development. The Cowboys could receive some reinforcements at linebacker, with Dee Winters progressing from limited participation Wednesday to a full practice Thursday. Winters' potential return would be particularly helpful with DeMarvion Overshown being limited with hamstring and back issues. Meanwhile, Marist Liufau has also returned to full participation as he works through his 21-day return-to-practice window, potentially giving Dallas another option at linebacker. The secondary is another area worth monitoring. Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke both progressed from not participating Wednesday to limited participation Thursday while dealing with concussions, an encouraging sign for Dallas. Both players must complete the NFL's concussion return-to-participation protocol. Their return to practice is encouraging, but neither is guaranteed to be available Sunday. Joey Porter Jr. also went from a full participant on Wednesday to limited on Thursday with an ankle injury. With multiple defensive backs dealing with injuries, Dallas could be facing some significant depth concerns against Indianapolis. At tight end, Jake Ferguson has missed the first two practices of the week with an ankle injury, leaving his availability for Sunday in question. Luke Schoonmaker has been limited in consecutive practices while dealing with a groin injury, but his participation is an encouraging sign. Getting Schoonmaker back would be particularly important if Ferguson remains sidelined, as Dallas could otherwise be severely shorthanded. The Cowboys also have some questions at wide receiver, where George Pickens has been limited for two consecutive days with a hamstring injury. His continued participation is encouraging, but his status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday. KaVontae Turpin, meanwhile, has missed both practices with a rib injury. His potential absence would affect both the receiving corps and special teams, where he provides an explosive return option. home.headline: Cowboys injury report: Overshown’s latest setback, Pickens and Porter Jr. updates
home.blurb: But the Cowboys won't be going into this game fully staffed either. Earlier this week, fans learned that Malachi Lawrence would be out for several weeks with an ankle injury, but he's not the only one in danger of missing this weekend's contest. Let's check out the latest regarding DeMarvion Overshown, George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr., Caleb Downs and others. On Friday, Schotteheimer told 105.3 The Fan that they needed to "get him out there today and see how he does.” Overshown is questionable after being limited the last two days. It always seems to be something with him, unfortunately, so fans won't hold their breath for Overshown to be active. Pickens has been dealing with a multitude of injuries this year, it seems, which at least partially explains his downturn in production. He was limited in all three practices leading up to the Colts game, and he is also questionable for Sunday. Dallas knew Porter Jr. was not 100% upon his arrival, but he's been a mainstay on the injury report and a full-on question mark every week, it feels like. He was full on Wednesday but has been limited the last two days, which is a bit worrisome, but Porter Jr. is questionable for Week 9. Schottenheimer said before Friday's practice that he was "hopeful" to have both Pickens and Porter Jr. against Indianapolis. Fans will find out Sunday morning if that was just wishful thinking. After missing the last two-plus games, Dee Winters will return for Dallas. The Cowboys have not had a fully healthy linebacker corps for an entire game this season, and if Overshown misses Sunday, it will remain that way. But for the time being, he is at least insurance if Overshown is out. Jake Ferguson improved from a non-participant on Wednesday and Thursday to being limited on Friday. It remains to be seen if he can play through his ankle injury, but he is officially questionable. Of course, Malachi Lawrence is out with the aforementioned ankle injury, and Kavontae Turpin will miss his third straight game with an injury to his ribs. Jonathan Bullard and Marist Liufau have not been activated to the 53-man roster, but they both practiced in full all week. Officially, they are questionable as the Cowboys mull over their roster math equations. Rapid fire: Luke Schoonmaker is questionable. Tyler Smith and Kenny Clark are good to go. The Dallas Cowboys' season already feels like it is on the ropes in Week 9 as they travel to take on one of the only teams in the NFL that are spiraling worse than they are: the Indianapolis Colts. And this is a get-right game if I've ever seen one, or if that even matters for Brian Schottenheimer's team. Indianapolis has already sold off great veterans like Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and word on the street is that Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, and maybe more, could be next. The vibes are certainly low in the Colts' locker room, and some "business decisions" could be made on Sunday. Dallas Cowboys injury update before Week 9 game vs. Indianapolis Colts

home.headline: Cowboys Offer Worrisome Injury Update Ahead Of Crucial 49ers Showdown
home.blurb: With the San Francisco 49ers up next, the Cowboys need everyone available to even have a shot at what would be an upset win in Week 10. "Busy week in the training room for us," Schottenheimer said. "PJ Locke will not be available this week. Jake Ferguson and Tyler Goodson should both miss multiple weeks. We're working through that. "[Donovan] Ezeiruaku, he's got an ankle sprain. See how he does. [Jonathan] Mingo, [KaVontae] Turpin, GP [Pickens], and JPJ [Joey Porter] try to get them back out there this week working, and see how they do. It was a busy day in the training room." Then Pickens and Porter Jr. appear, at least right now, to be questionable, while it isn't known if linebacker DeMarvion Overshown will be available, although he did look in good condition running onto the field to celebrate a Shemar James fumble recovery, which Schottenheimer called "unacceptable." Already in a hole, Dallas, while at home, will be up against it as Kyle Shanahan's team has made a habit of making an example out of the Cowboys over the years. The hope is that as the week goes on, it'll start to clear out. home.headline: Cowboys Injury Roundup: 'Tough decisions' ahead as Ferguson, Locke, others get bad news
home.source: Dallas Cowboys | Official Site of the Dallas Cowboys
home.blurb: FRISCO, Texas — Roughly two weeks ago, the Dallas Cowboys were feeling great about their injury report as key players began to get healthy and return to the practice and playing field. In the blink of an eye, they're suddenly back to having a lengthy and growing list of injuries that will again cost them impact players going forward. PJ Locke missed time this season before returning and suffering a concussion in Week 8, clearing protocol ahead of the matchup against the Indianapolis Colts before suffering a second concussion in as many weeks and, this time, he will not return in only a week's time. On Monday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer and the Cowboys officially ruled Locke out of the looming contest against the San Francisco 49ers — a sign he will likely miss multiple games. It was a scary sight to see Locke lying motionless for several moments before being helped to the sideline and not being permitted to return at Lucas Oil Stadium. Turpin will join DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back), George Pickens (hamstring) and Joey Porter Jr. (ankle), those three were ruled out ahead of kickoff against the Colts, in the rehab group this week to determine if either of them can go against the 49ers. And with Ferguson down, the expectation is that Luke Schoonmaker will return from injury to help with the currently ailing tight end depth chart. And though Marist Liufau was activated from injured reserve last week, Malachi Lawrence recently joined Thompson on IR, leaving the Cowboys with only one IR-DTR (designated to return) spot this regular season, assuming Lawrence returns as expected. That means if Ferguson, Goodson and Locke are moved to IR, only one of them would be allowed to return unless the Cowboys make the playoffs. On the day of the NFL's trade deadline, Cowboys owner/GM Jerry Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that he is not expecting Dallas to make a significant trade, "but don't count it out." In pulling out a much-needed win in Indianapolis, the Cowboys seemingly took craziness to a whole new level. After challenging his defense to execute for a full 60 minutes, Quinnen Williams led by example with a dominant performance that helped the Cowboys finish strong and close out a crucial victory. The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. Mike Tomlin backs Steelers pass rush to challenge Joe Burrow and Cincinnati Bengals Tomlin made no secret of his excitement when discussing the matchup, admitting he would be more than happy to make the trip to Cincinnati. Pittsburgh will arrive with plenty of confidence after enjoying a bye week. The Steelers' four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. away.headline: Ex-Steelers HC Mike Tomlin Leaves Door Open for Coaching Return
away.blurb: Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin isn't thinking about his future in coaching at the moment, though he at least kept the door open for a return in that regard. Tomlin is a Future Hall of Famer, Even if He Doesn't Return to Coaching The Steelers lost seven straight postseason games under Tomlin to close out his run with the team, but that shouldn't take away from the fact that he won Super Bowl XLIII with them in 2008 in addition to notching seven additional victories over 13 total trips to the playoffs. If Tomlin does decide to jump into the coaching carousel, whether that be in 2027, 2028 or beyond, there's some uncertainty around whether or not Pittsburgh would be able to trade his rights and receive assets in return. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/steelers/onsi as Ex-Steelers HC Mike Tomlin Leaves Door Open for Coaching Return . During a conference call with NBC correspondents before the Steelers ' Week 10 road matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football, which Tomlin will be in attendance for as part of the network's "Football Night in America" crew, he stated that he hasn't "given one iota" of thought towards returning to an NFL sideline while admitting that it is a topic of discussion that will likely pop up down the line. "I haven’t given one iota of thought to coaching," Tomlin said. "I’m sure some of that is going to come up in the not-so-distant future. But I’ll cross that bridge when I get there." While the end of his tenure with the Steelers wasn't always smooth, Tomlin's overall body of work with the franchise will undoubtedly be enough to make the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the future. In his 19 years at the helm in Pittsburgh before stepping down after the 2025 campaign, not once did Tomlin finish with a losing record while compiling an overall record of 193-114-2 in the regular season. Tied for the ninth-most head coaching wins in NFL history with fellow Pittsburgh legend Chuck Noll, Tomlin's legendary resume will always stand tall regardless of if he takes another job in the coming years or not. How Tomlin's Eventual Coaching Decision Could Impact Steelers The New Orleans Saints were able to do so when Sean Payton stepped away after the 2021 season and was later hired by the Denver Broncos in 2023, but it's unknown if the Steelers can follow suit. Should Pittsburgh still retain his contractual rights, it could potentially land a first-round pick (if not more) for Tomlin's services from whichever team hires him, which would greatly aid the organization's potential pursuit of a franchise quarterback. Even if the Steelers can't trade Tomlin, his destination in the event that he returns to coaching could impact the team if he takes a job in the AFC and thus would have to face the black and gold semi-frequently. away.blurb: Head coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. and defensive lineman Derrick Harmon are “getting close” to returning, per Nick Farabaugh . That said, McCarthy did not provide a definitive answer on whether either player would be available this week. Pittman has been sidelined with a foot injury that has interrupted his first season in Pittsburgh. Acquired from the Indianapolis Colts during the offseason, Pittman was expected to provide another reliable receiving option alongside DK Metcalf. home.headline: Injured Bengals Defender Good to Go Against Falcons as Team Announces Inactives
home.blurb: Johnson was listed as questionable on the injury report with an ankle/foot designation after suffering the injury in last week’s 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans. Safety Kyle Dugger was ruled out Friday with the quad injury that has forced him to miss three of the last four games. Cornerback DJ Turner II injured his foot last week against the Titans and was limited to start the week, but he did not appear on the injury report and is expected to start and play his full role. Injured Bengals Defender Good to Go Against Falcons as Team Announces Inactives Skip to main content SI.COM Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Cedric Johnson is active for today’s NFL International Game in Madrid against the Atlanta Falcons. The other inactives are offensive tackle Myles Hinton, center Connor Lew and defensive tackle Landon Robinson. The Bengals only need four inactives today because their roster is currently at 52. The Bengals arrived in Madrid on Wednesday and practiced Thursday and Friday to get back on a normal weekly schedule. "I think this is the best compromise we found to make sure that we can get acclimated by Friday, get a really good practice where we feel better, and then play our best on Sunday," head coach Zac Taylor said on Thursday. "So we've all embraced that mindset, and I think it's working well for us so far." "We're back on schedule,” he added. “Our meetings were the same as they've always been on Thursday. So today is more of a third-down emphasis with some normal downs, and then tomorrow will be red zone-based." Quarterback Joe Burrow said he and his teammates are excited to be representing the NFL abroad and about being in a stand-alone window as the only game on Sunday morning. “It means a lot to me that we're here,” he said Friday. “I think this is Year 7 for me, and I haven't been overseas yet. And we keep adding more and more games to try to build the NFL globally. I think it's worked over the last five years, and I'm hoping to add more and continue to build, and I love being part of that, and I want to help grow the game, and so I love being here. "I love being the only game on TV on Sunday morning when people back home wake up, and I love showcasing our talents abroad and trying to bring attention to what we do, as far as what our offense brings. I think we're explosive, we're dynamic, we're fun to watch, and I think we're going to put on a show on Sunday." The team will fly home immediately after the game and, unlike their previous two international games when they had a bye to recover, will start preparations for a key AFC North game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. November 10, 2026 / 4:51 PM EST / CBS Baltimore The Baltimore Ravens are in need of a kicker after the Atlanta Falcons reportedly poached Jake Moody from their practice squad on Tuesday. Moody is signing with the Falcons and will be added to their 53-man roster, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Moody was elevated to the Ravens' active roster ahead of their 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Nov. 5, making a 53-yard field goal in the game. Moody joined the Ravens' practice squad twice this season as the team looked for competition for struggling kicker Tyler Loop. Loop was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury and will miss at least the next three games. He has converted 13 of 17 field goal attempts this season, including just two of five attempts from 40 to 49 yards. However, Loop has also made kicks from 57 and 64 yards, with the latter securing a win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. Moody rejoined Baltimore's practice squad on Oct. 19 and appeared in one game for the Ravens. Now, the Ravens (4-5), who sit in last place in the AFC North, must find another kicker and add him to their 53-man roster before their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football, Nov. 16.

home.headline: Lamar Jackson's Message to Ravens Revealed in NFL Rumors amid Injury, Return Buzz and Losing Streak
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is aiming to return during the 2026 NFL season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . After playing the first three games of the year, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain, returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Buffalo Bills. His return was brief, however, as he suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive drive. Rapoport reported that Jackson spoke to the team and delivered an "energizing" and "exciting" message. The overall theme was to "just stay alive" until he's healthy enough to be back on the field. The Ravens are last in the AFC North at 4-5 following Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The combined absences of Jackson and Tyler Huntley were glaring as third-stringer Joe Fagnano threw for 60 yards and two interceptions on 18 attempts. Jackson has unfortunately had another injury-riddled year. The injury required surgery, and the two-time MVP was placed on the injured reserve immediately after the game. Huntley came in for Jackson after his injury, but he was forced to exit soon after because of a turf toe injury. A day after the Jaguars loss, Baltimore acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett is a significant upgrade from Fagnano and may be enough for the team to keep its head above water in the weeks ahead. It's clear Jackson isn't throwing away the rest of the season, and that attitude is bound to spread to the rest of the locker room.

home.headline: Desperate Baltimore Ravens seal huge NFL quarterback trade after Jackson and Huntley injuries
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens have found a fix to their quarterback injury woes by trading for Arizona Cardinals star Jacoby Brissett. The Ravens are down to third-choice undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , leaving general manager Eric DaCosta desperately scrabbling around for a long-term solution. NFL insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report on Wednesday that the Ravens are now finalizing a trade for Brissett, with the deal set to be completed over the weekend. Fagnano will therefore be on the field for Baltimore on Thursday night, before Brissett takes the quarterback reins in Week 10 for the Monday Night Football showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett had become a prime trade candidate in Arizona after being benched midgame against the Dallas Cowboys and then dropped to QB3 on the depth chart. He started the first eight games of the season for Arizona this season, going 3-5 with a 63.3% pass completion. After Brissett was benched during the loss to the Cowboys, the starting job was handed to Gardner Minshew, with Carson Beck the backup. West Palm Beach native Brissett will join his seventh NFL team in Baltimore, in his 11th season in the league. He was first selected by the New England Patriots in the third round of the 2016 Draft, going on to win the Super Bowl as Tom Brady's backup in his first season. He was traded to the Colts after his rookie season and was the starter there in 2017 and 2019, before alternating as a back-up and starter in Miami, Cleveland, Washington and back in New England, before eventually landing in Arizona. In March 2025 he signed a two-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals and played in 14 games last season. Despite reworking his contract to increase his compensation for the 2026 season, he will become a free agent at the end of the campaign, unless he agrees new terms in Baltimore.

home.blurb: The Ravens have told Henry they do not intend to trade him, according to ESPN reporting summarized by Reuters. Lamar Jackson’s return hopes influence Ravens’ outlook Jackson reportedly told teammates he intends to return later this season after suffering a fractured and dislocated right thumb. Rapoport reported a six-to-nine-week absence, leaving uncertainty about when the quarterback could become available. The possibility provides context for Baltimore’s decision to acquire Brissett. The Ravens need to remain competitive long enough for a potential Jackson return to matter, rather than assuming his injury has ended their season. The Brissett acquisition and reported decision to retain Henry show Baltimore is continuing to invest in its chances this season. They don't guarantee another addition or rule out an individual departure. The NFL trade deadline is one day away, and the 4-5 Baltimore Ravens have already addressed their most urgent need. Baltimore acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett from Arizona after injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley depleted the position. Brissett’s arrival gives the Ravens an experienced starter as they attempt to end a four-game losing streak and remain in the AFC playoff race. The quarterback addition does not answer every roster question. Derrick Henry reportedly has been told the Ravens intend to keep him, while the Giants have inquired about fellow running back Justice Hill. We will track the latest Ravens trade news, rumors, and completed deals on this page through Tuesday’s deadline. The reported decision also suggests Baltimore isn't treating its losing streak as a reason to automatically move its most established players. Arizona also paid more than half of Brissett’s remaining salary, according to Ian Rapoport’s reporting, which the Ravens cited. Brissett is slated to start against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16. home.headline: Ravens lose kicker Jake Moody to Falcons, must find replacement before Chargers game
home.blurb: The former third-round draft pick out of Michigan was subsequently returned to Baltimore's practice squad before being claimed by Atlanta. November 10, 2026 / 4:51 PM EST / CBS Baltimore The Baltimore Ravens are in need of a kicker after the Atlanta Falcons reportedly poached Jake Moody from their practice squad on Tuesday. Moody is signing with the Falcons and will be added to their 53-man roster, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Moody was elevated to the Ravens' active roster ahead of their 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Nov. 5, making a 53-yard field goal in the game. Moody joined the Ravens' practice squad twice this season as the team looked for competition for struggling kicker Tyler Loop. Loop was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury and will miss at least the next three games. He has converted 13 of 17 field goal attempts this season, including just two of five attempts from 40 to 49 yards. However, Loop has also made kicks from 57 and 64 yards, with the latter securing a win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. Moody rejoined Baltimore's practice squad on Oct. 19 and appeared in one game for the Ravens. Now, the Ravens (4-5), who sit in last place in the AFC North, must find another kicker and add him to their 53-man roster before their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football, Nov. 16.

home.headline: Ravens release Nick Vannett, Kyle Hergel in roster shakeup
home.blurb: Hergel was promoted from the practice squad Oct. 25 after being elevated for three previous games. His departure comes as Baltimore adds Neuzil, an experienced interior offensive lineman who can play center and guard. The Ravens also have Chuma Edoga and Emery Jones available as reserve offensive linemen. The Baltimore Ravens continued reshaping their roster Tuesday, releasing tight end Nick Vannett and guard Kyle Hergel from the 53-man roster. Baltimore also released veteran guard Michael Jordan from the practice squad and brought back fullback Lucas Scott, who was signed to the practice squad. The Ravens announced all four transactions shortly after acquiring offensive lineman Ryan Neuzil from the Atlanta Falcons. The moves give Baltimore more flexibility ahead of its Monday night matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. They also represent another adjustment to an offensive depth chart repeatedly altered by injuries and transactions. Nick Vannett’s brief Ravens tenure ends Baltimore initially added Vannett to the practice squad before signing him to the active roster Oct. 7, the same day tight end Durham Smythe was placed on injured reserve with an Achilles injury. Vannett provided an experienced blocking option behind Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas. The 32-year-old has appeared in more than 100 regular-season games since the Seattle Seahawks selected him in the third round of the 2016 NFL draft. His release could create additional opportunities for Baltimore’s younger tight ends while making room for another position on the active roster. Lucas Scott returns to practice squad Jordan’s second stint with Baltimore lasted approximately two weeks. The Ravens signed him to the practice squad Oct. 27, giving the team an experienced guard while it navigated injuries along the offensive line. Scott is returning eight days after Baltimore released him from the practice squad. His versatility as a fullback and tight end gives the Ravens another developmental option who can contribute to the running game and special teams. The Ravens’ official transaction history shows Vannett joined the active roster Oct. 7, Hergel was promoted Oct. 25, and Jordan signed with the practice squad Oct. 27. Baltimore could make more roster moves before facing Los Angeles, especially after creating two openings on the 53-man roster while adding only Neuzil.
